Why Uluwatu.

For the wider case on why investors choose Bali , our investment guide covers the numbers in full.
Why Bali One of the world's most consistent short-term rental markets TripAdvisor's #1 destination five years running.
Seven million visitors annually.
Most rental markets have one good season.
Bali has four: wellness travellers in January, honeymooners in June, surfers July through October, families over Christmas.
Demand never fully drops - which is why the yield numbers actually hold up.
7M+ annual tourists 12-18% projected yields Why Uluwatu Bali's fastest-growing premium address Uluwatu has outpaced the rest of Bali for five straight years.
Savaya, Single Fin, the cliffs, the surf - it has its own draw now, separate from Bali broadly.
Guests book Uluwatu specifically and pay more because of it.
Those same cliffs also mean there's a hard ceiling on how much supply can ever come to market.

85%+ peak occupancy 15-20% off-plan appreciation Why Wellness The fastest-growing travel category, designed in from day one Wellness tourism has grown 40% faster than general tourism over the last decade.
Guests who are there for the sauna and cold plunge stay longer, spend more, and write the kind of reviews that fill future calendars.
Every Suku 4-bedroom comes with its own sauna and ice bath, the 3-bedroom can add them, and butler service is included with every villa.

Investor Questions Everything You Need to Know Buying property overseas is a serious decision.
The main questions are covered below.
For anything more specific, our team is on WhatsApp and responds fast.
Ask Us on WhatsApp What is Suku Residences and what makes it different?
+ Suku Residences is a boutique villa community in Uluwatu, Bali - 3 to 4 bedroom private pool villas with dedicated butler service, beach shuttle, and 24/7 security included as standard.
Each villa can also have its own sauna and ice bath: they are included with the 4-bedroom and available as an option on the 3-bedroom.
What are the prices for Suku Residences?
+ Suku starts from $355,000 USD for a 3-bedroom villa, with the 4-bedroom flagship above it.
The 2-bedroom villas are sold out.
Off-plan pricing is typically below completed market value - early buyers lock in the lower price before construction completion.
When will Suku Residences be completed?
+ Construction begins in early 2026.
Completion is scheduled for mid 2027.
As an off-plan purchase, your payment schedule is tied to construction milestones.
You receive regular site updates and progress documentation throughout the build.
Is Suku Residences in Bali's Pink Zone?
+ Yes.
Suku Residences is Pink Zone compliant - meaning it has the correct zoning and licensing to operate legally as a short-term rental villa.
This is not a minor detail.
Pink Zone compliance protects your ability to rent commercially and shields the investment against regulatory enforcement.
Not all developments in Uluwatu carry this compliance.
Can foreigners purchase at Suku Residences?
The standard structure is a 30-year leasehold with a 30-year extension option - 60 years total - available directly to foreign individuals.
Buying through a PT PMA company, which holds a right-to-build title (Hak Guna Bangunan), is also an option for buyers who prefer that structure.
Both are established, legally sound routes for international investors in Bali.
What rental yields can I expect?
+ Uluwatu is currently Bali's best-performing short-term rental market.
Villas with wellness amenities - sauna, cold plunge, butler service - consistently outperform standard tropical builds on nightly rate and occupancy.
Suku's positioning puts it in a premium tier on Airbnb and Booking.com.
Formal yield projections by configuration are available from the sales team.
Can I personalise my villa?
+ As an off-plan purchase, limited personalisation is available during the design phase - finishes, fixtures, and minor layout adjustments.
Once construction reaches lock-up stage, changes are no longer practical.
Contact us early in the process if customisation is a priority.
What is the lease term?
+ 30 years with a 30-year extension option - 60 years total.
This is Balitecture's standard leasehold structure, drawn up by qualified Indonesian notaries and registered to protect the buyer's position throughout the full lease period.

CORE Villas is a boutique collection of seventeen architect-designed villas in Seseh, Munggu, on Bali’s fast-rising west coast.
Minutes from the beach, Pererenan and Canggu: connected to Bali’s best dining, schools and wellness, with the quiet, easy rhythm you actually want at home.
Each villa is designed for effortless tropical living, with generous interiors that open onto a private pool and landscaped garden.

Offered off-plan in three and four bedroom layouts on private plots of 358 to 451 m², with total built areas of up to 358 m², and the option of the curated furniture & appliance package for fully turnkey delivery.
The investment case The investment case The Community A proper residential community.
Core Villas is a neighbourhood designed to fit around your life rather than ask you to fit around it.
Most of Bali’s villa market is organised around the short let, with new guests every few days.
This one is organised around the people who own the homes and the residents who live in them.
A villa here works three ways, and you can move between them as your circumstances change.
Live in it as your permanent home.
Keep it as your place in Bali and return to a house that is maintained, cleaned and ready whenever you land.
Or let it to long-stay residents while you are away, so it earns rather than sits empty.
Management is based on site.
The pool, the garden, the tenancy and the paperwork are handled to the same standard whether you are in residence or not.
Your neighbours have chosen the same arrangement, which is why the place stays quiet.

The point is a home that adapts to the phase of life you are in: a first base to settle into, a holiday retreat to come back to, or an investment that earns while you are elsewhere, with the freedom to move between them as things change.
That is rare on this coast, and it is deliberate.
Anyone can build a villa here.
This is the model that holds the quality of life.

The Bingin sub-market has sustained strong short-term rental demand driven by international surf tourism, proximity to Uluwatu's luxury hotel corridor, and the area's growing appeal among digital nomads and long-stay visitors.
Pricing is not publicly disclosed, preventing direct price-per-sqm benchmarking; based on comparable Bingin leasehold off-plan listings, the market typically ranges IDR 3.5–7B for 2BR villas.
Developer identity is also not publicly confirmed, which is the primary due diligence gap buyers must resolve before committing.

Pros 59-year effective leasehold (29+30yr) — significantly above Bali's 25–30yr market standard Private 7m infinity pools — essential filter for premium short-term rental bookings Gated community structure — 24/7 security with controlled access Modular bedroom design — flexibility to adapt between guest and office use 12-month build with staged payments — capital efficiency for off-plan buyers Considerations Developer identity not publicly disclosed — track record cannot be verified independently No official project name — may complicate title documentation and resale marketing Pricing not published — requires direct agent engagement before any financial analysis 170 sqm land plots are compact — outdoor space limited for a 2BR villa Bingin is subject to legal scrutiny regarding villa development permits — verify IMB status carefully Recommended For Short-term rental investors targeting Bingin/Uluwatu's proven surf-tourism demand Buyers seeking maximum effective leasehold tenure (59 years) in the Bukit Peninsula Digital nomad lifestyle buyers wanting a gated community with work-from-home flexibility Not Recommended For Investors requiring verified developer identity before committing (developer unnamed) Buyers needing more than 170 sqm of land (compact plots) Buyers concerned about Bingin's permit environment (verify IMB before purchase) Risk Assessment Developer risk — identity unconfirmed; no track record verification High Permit risk — Bingin zoning has faced scrutiny; IMB verification is critical Medium Demand risk — Bingin surf-tourism rental market is well-established Low Leasehold risk — 59yr effective tenure is among the best in this sub-market Low Overview Bingin Ocean Villas is a private gated community of 33 designer villas in Bingin, Uluwatu — one of Bali's most established surf and lifestyle addresses on the southern Bukit Peninsula.

Each villa is positioned on 170 square metres of leasehold land with a 29-year primary lease term and a 30-year extension option, providing a total effective tenure of 59 years — among the strongest leasehold structures available in the Uluwatu sub-market at this price tier and a meaningful differentiator from the 25-year standard that remains common across comparable Bingin developments.
The development delivers two-bedroom villas with a ground-floor bedroom layout, built-in wardrobes, and premium bathrooms.

The second bedroom is designed as a modular space convertible between a guest room and home office configuration — a deliberate nod to the digital nomad and remote-work segment that represents a growing share of Bingin's longer-stay rental demand.
Living areas feature a sunken lounge, separate dining area, and open-concept kitchen with modern appliances.

Each villa includes a private infinity pool measuring 7 metres in length, with large sliding glass panels integrating the interior with the outdoor terrace and pool deck to maximise the indoor-outdoor connection that consistently drives premium nightly rates on rental platforms.

The project's gated community structure provides 24-hour security and controlled access — an increasingly valued feature among both owner-occupiers and yield-focused investors in Bingin, where the combination of surf-break proximity and cliffside terrain has historically constrained land supply.

What Determines Prices Of Property in Bali The same budget can give buyers access to very different types of property in Bali, from compact apartments near the ocean to more spacious properties in less tourist-oriented areas.
That is why several factors should be considered when comparing options.
The main factors that influence the price are: location and distance from the beach; property type and size; stage of construction; leasehold term; project quality and infrastructure.
Location and Proximity to the Beach Location is especially important for buyers who plan to buy property in Bali and rent it out.
Properties in Canggu, Berawa, Seminyak, and Uluwatu usually cost more because these areas are in high demand among tourists and investors.
Proximity to the ocean and urban infrastructure also affects the price.
Property Type How much property in Bali costs largely depends on the type of property.
Studios, apartments, and villas fall into different price segments.
The price is influenced by the size, number of bedrooms, layout, private pool or terrace, as well as the features of the complex itself.
Stage of Construction Property in Bali includes both completed properties and projects at different stages of construction.
Prices are often lower at an early stage than after the project is completed.
At the same time, it is important to assess the developer’s experience, stated completion dates, and previously delivered projects.
Leasehold Term The decision to buy property in Bali on a leasehold basis requires careful consideration of the contract term.
The longer the remaining leasehold period, the longer the buyer has the right to use the property, which also affects its value.
Project Level The infrastructure of the complex also affects property price.
A swimming pool, fitness area, spa, workspace, restaurant, parking, and security increase the cost of developing and maintaining the project and may place it in a higher price segment.
How Much Does Property in Bali Cost in 2026?
There is no single market price for property in Bali: the cost depends on the property type, size, location, and stage of construction.
In 2026, prices start at around $100,000 for compact apartments, while villas generally require a larger budget.
Apartment Prices in Bali in 2026 How much does property in Bali cost?
At the more affordable end of the market, apartment prices in Bali in 2026 start at around $100,000 for compact units and selected properties at the construction stage.
One-bedroom apartments are most commonly priced between $120,000 and $200,000, while larger two-bedroom units may cost from $180,000–200,000 and above.
Premium apartments are usually more expensive due to their larger size, amenities provided, complex infrastructure, and location.
Prices for such properties can cost more than $300,000.
How Much Does a Villa in Bali Cost?
A villa in Bali represents a separate price segment.
According to industry data, the median price of villas on the island is approximately $256,000–299,000.

Depending on the property class: smaller villas may cost less than the median price; two- or three-bedroom villas with more space and a private plot often cost $300,000–600,000 or more; premium properties can cost over $500,000, while large high-end villas may reach $1 million or more.
Property Prices in Different Areas of Bali One of the key features of the market for property in Bali is the noticeable difference in prices across different parts of the island.
In some areas, prices are supported by stable tourist demand, while in others the main factors are limited land availability or proximity to the ocean.
Canggu and Berawa High rental demand is one of the reasons why many investors choose to buy property in Bali specifically in Canggu and Berawa.
These areas already have well-developed infrastructure for living and leisure, including restaurants, beach clubs, international schools, and fitness centres.
This supports demand for both short-term and long-term rentals.
Uluwatu Uluwatu clearly shows how much real estate prices can depend on the exact location.
The terrain of the peninsula varies considerably, so land with ocean views or convenient access to popular beaches can cost significantly more than plots farther inland in Bukit.
Seminyak A villa in Bali in an established tourist area such as Seminyak can be more expensive because of dense development and the limited availability of vacant land.
At the same time, well-developed tourism infrastructure helps maintain stable demand for property in the area.
Other Areas of Bali Buyers who are willing to buy an apartment or a villa in Bali outside the main tourist centres have a wider range of options.
Pererenan is developing alongside neighbouring Canggu, while Ubud is more focused on quiet stays, long-term living, and wellness tourism.
In less developed areas, prices may be lower, but tourism infrastructure is usually more limited.
How Property Prices in Bali Are Changing in 2026 Overall market trends are also affecting apartment prices in Bali in 2026.
According to industry analysis, prices have increased by around 7% over the past year, although the pace of growth varies significantly depending on the quality and location of the project.
At the same time, supply is increasing.
Around 4,260 new residential units are expected to be completed on the island in 2026, increasing competition between projects.
Buyers are paying closer attention to: construction quality; the infrastructure and amenities of the complex; location; property management terms.
Demand is also supported by strong tourist arrivals.
In April 2026 alone, Bali welcomed more than 553,000 international visitors.
This continues to support interest in properties designed for both short-term and long-term rentals.
Conclusion For buyers, property in Bali in 2026 offers a wide range of options with differences in price and features.
The final budget depends on the area, property type, stage of construction, and leasehold term.
The choice of developer in Bali is equally important: their experience, the quality of completed projects, and ability to meet deadlines directly affect the reliability of the purchase.
Compact apartments remain the most affordable option, while villas and premium properties require a significantly larger budget.
Growing supply is giving buyers more choice and making the market more competitive.
When comparing properties, it is therefore important to consider the project’s features, location, and potential for future rental income.

How to Buy Real Estate in Bali as a Foreigner What Foreigners Need to Know in 2026 to Buy Real Estate in Bali Interest in Bali real estate remains strong, but so does the number of questions from international buyers.
Today, people are looking beyond the price of a villa, flat, or off-plan apartments in Bali.
They also want to understand how the purchase process works, which ownership options are available to foreigners, and what costs to expect before and after signing the contract.
If you plan to buy real estate in Bali as a foreigner, it is important to know that the legal framework differs significantly from many European countries.
Foreigners can legally purchase property in Bali, but they cannot own land under freehold title in their own name.

Before choosing a property, it is worth understanding: whether foreigners can buy property in Bali and which ownership structures are available; how the transaction works from selecting a property to completing the legal documentation; the total cost of purchasing property, including additional fees; which property taxes should be taken into account; which legal documents should be verified before paying a deposit.
In 2026, the key question is no longer simply which villa to choose.
It is how to structure the transaction in a transparent, secure way that matches your investment goals.
Can Foreigners Buy Property in Bali?
One of the first questions buyers ask is whether a foreigner can purchase a villa or apartment in Bali and register it in their own name.
The short answer is yes, but Bali real estate for foreigners is subject to specific legal restrictions and ownership rules.
Foreigners cannot obtain Hak Milik, the Indonesian freehold title available only to Indonesian citizens.
This is why the common phrase "buying a villa in Bali" is not the same as owning land under Indonesian law.
Foreign buyers can use the property, invest in it, rent it out, or transfer their rights, but only within the legal ownership structures available to them.

In practice, foreigners can buy property in Bali through several legal options: Leasehold — a long-term lease of land or property; Hak Pakai — the right to use a property; PT PMA — acquiring eligible property rights and conducting commercial activities through a foreign-owned company registered in Indonesia.
The right option depends on your investment goals.
One ownership structure may be suitable for a private residence, another for a rental business, and another for long-term investment or resale.
That is why, before signing a purchase agreement, it is essential to evaluate not only the property, location, and price but also the legal rights you will receive after the transaction is completed.

Bali Real Estate for Foreigners: Available Ownership Options For foreign buyers, purchasing property in Bali is typically based on either a legal right to use the property or ownership through a specific legal structure.
The option you choose determines how long you can hold the property, whether you can rent it out, and the conditions for selling or transferring your rights in the future.
It is important to distinguish between the three main ownership structures: Leasehold, Hak Pakai, and PT PMA.
These are not different versions of the same purchase method but separate legal mechanisms with different rights, timeframes, restrictions, and purposes.
Leasehold: Long-Term Lease Leasehold is one of the most common options in Bali real estate for foreigners.
In practice, it is a long-term lease of land or a property rather than freehold ownership.
There is no standard lease term for every transaction.
While agreements of 25–30 years are common, the exact duration is negotiated between the parties and specified in the contract.
This option is suitable for buyers who plan to use the property as a private residence, a holiday home, or a rental investment.
However, the lease agreement itself is the most important document in the transaction.

Before signing, make sure to review: the lease term; extension conditions; the cost of extending the lease; whether the lease rights can be transferred to another buyer; restrictions on the use of the property; what happens to the building when the lease expires; the responsibilities of each party.
Leasehold can be a practical ownership structure, but its security depends largely on the quality of the contract and proper legal due diligence.
Hak Pakai: Registered Right of Use Hak Pakai is a registered right to use property in Indonesia.
It may be available to foreign buyers who meet specific legal requirements, including holding the appropriate immigration documents and having a valid legal status in Indonesia.
Hak Pakai is generally intended for buyers who want to use the property primarily as their private residence or for personal purposes.
It is important to understand that the right to use a property does not automatically grant the right to operate it as a short-term rental or commercial investment.
If your goal is to rent out a villa, this should be verified before completing the purchase with a qualified lawyer, notary, or licensed property consultant in Indonesia.
They should review the property's legal documentation, land zoning, permitted land use, ownership registration, and whether the required licenses for rental activities can be obtained.
Otherwise, you may discover that the property is perfectly suitable for private use but cannot legally be rented to tourists.
Hak Pakai may provide stronger legal protection than a standard lease agreement.
However, if your objective is Bali real estate investment or generating rental income, this ownership structure should be evaluated carefully.
In many cases, another legal structure, such as PT PMA, may be more appropriate.
PT PMA: Buying Property Through a Company PT PMA is an Indonesian company with foreign ownership.
Through this legal entity, foreign investors can acquire eligible property rights and conduct commercial activities in Indonesia.
For those planning to buy real estate in Bali as a foreigner, PT PMA is not a way to "buy a villa in your own name." It is a business structure designed for commercial operations.
This option may be suitable if you plan to rent out the property, manage rental income, or hold it as an investment asset.
It is important to understand that establishing a PT PMA does not grant a foreigner Hak Milik (freehold ownership of land).
This title is available only to Indonesian citizens.
A PT PMA can hold only those property rights that are permitted under Indonesian law.
For a rental business, registering a PT PMA alone is not enough.
It is also essential to verify the company's business activities, required licenses, land zoning, permits, and whether the property rights have been structured correctly.
For this reason, a PT PMA can be an effective solution for implementing a commercial investment strategy, but it is not always necessary for purchasing property for private use.

Step-by-Step Process to Buy Property in Bali To buy real estate in Bali safely, it is important to view the process not as a quick property selection, but as a structured transaction supported by proper legal due diligence.
Most mistakes happen not when choosing a villa or apartment, but when buyers rush to pay a deposit or do not fully understand the ownership structure.
The process typically includes the following steps: Define your investment goal.
A property for personal use, rental income, long-term investment, or resale may require different legal structures.
Choose the location and budget.

At this stage, it is important not only to understand property prices in Bali but also to calculate the total cost of the transaction, including the property type, ownership structure, project stage, taxes, legal fees, and future maintenance costs.
Select the appropriate ownership structure.
Determine whether Leasehold, Hak Pakai, or PT PMA best fits your objectives.
Conduct legal due diligence.
Verify the land title, ownership documents, permits, zoning regulations, and the developer's reputation.
Review the purchase agreement and payment terms.
Pay particular attention to the deposit, completion timeline, lease extension terms, transfer of rights, and the responsibilities of each party.
Sign the transaction documents before a notary or PPAT.
Pay the applicable taxes and government fees.
Receive the final ownership documents and, if the property is intended for rental income, arrange professional property management.
Following this process helps you evaluate not only the property's investment potential but also the legal security of the transaction.

Bali Real Estate Investment: Taxes and Costs Every Buyer Should Consider One of the first questions buyers ask is: "can foreigners buy property in Bali?" Once they have the answer, many focus primarily on the purchase price.
In reality, the total cost of ownership goes far beyond the price of a villa or apartment and includes legal fees, due diligence, taxes, and ongoing maintenance expenses.
It is important to understand that Bali property tax is not a single, universal payment.

Property-related costs may arise at different stages of ownership: when acquiring property rights, during the transfer of ownership, throughout the ownership period, and when generating rental income.

Why is Bali Real Estate Increasing in Value?
Just a few years ago, buying property in Bali was mainly seen as an investment in holiday real estate.
Today, the market has evolved.
New residential developments continue to emerge across the island, infrastructure is expanding, and demand remains strong throughout the year, well beyond the peak tourist season.
What is driving property prices upward?
Let's look at the key factors.
Consistently strong rental demand One of the main reasons Bali property prices continue to rise is the island's strong rental market.
Throughout the year, Bali attracts tourists, entrepreneurs, families, and remote professionals from around the world.
Many of them are looking for more than a hotel room.
They prefer apartments or villas where they can stay for several weeks or even months.
This keeps both short-term and long-term rental demand high, particularly in Canggu, Pererenan, Seminyak, Ubud, and the Bukit Peninsula.
Limited supply of land Land available for development in Bali's most desirable locations is limited.
Plots close to the ocean, established amenities, and convenient transport routes are especially sought after.
As more land is developed, the number of available plots continues to shrink, pushing land prices higher.
This has a direct impact on the value of newly built villas and apartments.
Why location matters Even within the same area, property prices can vary significantly.

The value of a property depends on factors such as: distance from the beach; road access; nearby restaurants, shops, and fitness facilities; future development potential of the area; the level of competition among rental properties.
That is why properties in the best locations within the same neighbourhood often appreciate faster than those in less convenient areas.
Higher standards in new developments Today's buyers pay closer attention to architecture, layouts, interior finishes, and professional property management.
As a result, modern developments increasingly offer a wider range of on-site facilities and services.
New developments in Bali may include swimming pools, fitness centres, yoga studios, restaurants, lounge areas, and professional property management.
These projects require larger investments to develop, but they are better aligned with the expectations of international buyers and tenants.
As a result, they tend to remain more attractive for both rental income and future resale.
Growing interest from international investors Many investors view Bali real estate as an opportunity to generate rental income while benefiting from long-term capital appreciation.

The strongest demand is typically focused on projects that offer: prime tourist locations; professional property management; a clear and transparent legal structure; well-developed infrastructure; a realistic investment model.
Strong international demand also helps support property values across the market.
Which properties are more likely to appreciate?
Owning property in Bali alone does not guarantee future price growth.

The investment potential of a property depends on several factors working together, including: the popularity of the location; construction quality; property management standards; ongoing maintenance costs; rental demand; the level of competition from nearby properties.

A villa or apartment within a thoughtfully designed residential development may offer better long-term value than a larger standalone property with poor access, limited infrastructure, and no professional management.
Is buying property in Bali worth considering?
The Bali real estate market continues to grow, supported by strong tourism, limited land availability, and an increasing number of high-quality residential developments.
However, any purchase decision should be based on careful due diligence.
It is important to assess the location, legal documentation, ownership structure, the developer's reputation, maintenance costs, and expected rental returns.

Investment Guide in Bali for Beginners Investing in Bali real estate can be an attractive option for first-time buyers.
Consistent rental demand, ongoing infrastructure development, and the island’s popularity among tourists support interest in local property, particularly apartments.
Those planning to buy property in Bali should first understand the local market and the rules involved in completing a purchase.
This guide covers the main steps and key considerations involved in investing in Bali real estate.
Why invest in Bali real estate?
Bali benefits from steady rental demand due to its popularity among tourists and expats.
Areas such as Canggu offer a combination of leisure, developed infrastructure, and comfortable living, attracting both short-term visitors and long-term tenants.
Apartments can perform well across both rental markets, giving owners greater flexibility and access to a broader tenant base.
How to choose the right investment property?
When selecting a property in Bali, consider its price, rental demand, location, and potential for capital appreciation.
Apartments in popular areas such as Canggu often attract consistent interest from tenants and may be easier to resell than some other property types.
Developments with facilities such as swimming pools, co-working spaces, security, and underground parking can be more attractive to tenants and support stronger rental performance.
What returns can investors expect?
Rental returns depend on the location, property class, occupancy rate, seasonality, and quality of management.
Some apartment projects advertise rental yields of 10–15% per year, with potentially higher figures in the premium segment.
However, actual returns should be calculated after accounting for management fees, taxes, maintenance costs, and periods without tenants.
Buying an apartment during the construction stage may also provide an opportunity for capital appreciation once the project is completed.
Some developments project value growth of up to 20–30%, but these figures are not guaranteed and should be assessed against comparable properties and current market conditions.
What property ownership options are available in Bali?
One of the most common options for foreign investors is leasehold ownership, which grants the right to use a property for a period specified in the agreement.
Leasehold properties may be used personally or rented out, depending on the terms of the contract.
Before proceeding with a purchase, investors should check the remaining lease term, extension conditions, transfer rights, and permitted use of the property.
All documents should be reviewed by an independent local legal adviser.
What are the main maintenance costs?
Apartments are generally easier and more cost-efficient to manage than standalone villas.
In many developments, a property management company handles cleaning, repairs, security, and the upkeep of shared facilities such as swimming pools and common areas.
Owners may also need to cover utilities, management fees, routine maintenance, and contributions toward the operation of the development.
The total cost depends on the size of the apartment, the level of service, and the facilities available, so all regular fees should be confirmed before purchasing.
Taxes and legal considerations Taxes and transaction costs depend on the legal structure of the purchase, the ownership format, the property’s status, and the way rental income is received.
Expenses may include taxes related to the purchase or sale, tax on rental income, notary fees, and other administrative charges.
Before completing a transaction, investors should consult a local legal and tax specialist.
They can confirm the applicable rates, review the ownership structure, and calculate the full cost of purchasing and holding the property.
How can investors reduce risks?
To reduce risks, it is important to work with an established developer and an independent legal adviser.
Investors should verify the land documents, construction permits, contractual terms, project timeline, and the developer’s track record.
It is also worth assessing actual rental demand, competition in the area, management costs, and future infrastructure plans.
A popular location can support demand, but it does not guarantee a particular return or increase in property value.
How liquid is Bali real estate?
Apartments in popular areas, including Canggu, may attract interest on the resale market due to developed infrastructure and rental demand.
However, the time required to sell a property depends on its price, condition, location, remaining lease term, management quality, and current market conditions.
A well-positioned property can give investors more flexibility and may be easier to resell when necessary.
Before purchasing, it is useful to review comparable resale listings and understand how long similar properties typically remain on the market.
How to get started with property investment Begin by defining your budget, investment goals, preferred location, and property type.
Compare several projects, review their management terms, calculate all expected costs, and carry out an independent legal check before signing any agreement.
Apartments in Canggu may suit first-time investors due to the area’s popularity, developed infrastructure, and wide range of available projects.
Each property should still be assessed individually based on its financial projections, legal status, and market position.
For more information, contact our managers.
They will provide a free consultation and help you explore properties that match your budget and investment goals.
Apartments in Bali: The Best Choice for Investment When it comes to real estate in Bali, investors often find themselves torn between purchasing a villa, townhouse, or apartment.
However, when analyzing the advantages of each type of property, it becomes clear that apartments have unique features that make them more attractive to modern investors and renters.
Affordable Entry Cost and Low Investment Threshold Apartments in Bali offer a relatively low entry threshold into the real estate market.
This allows investors to acquire property with lower costs compared to villas or townhouses, leaving room for high potential returns.
Investors looking to minimize purchase and maintenance expenses will find apartments to be an optimal choice.
Minimal Maintenance and Clean Living Space One key aspect that sets apartments apart from villas and townhouses in Bali is the absence of certain “wildlife” that may appear in private yards.
Since apartments lack large open spaces, owners don’t have to worry about unwanted “neighbors” like snakes, geckos, frogs, and other animals common to greener and more open areas.
Investors and renters who prefer a clean environment will find apartments much more comfortable for living.
Convenient Underground Parking and Access to Modern Amenities Modern apartment complexes in Bali offer essential amenities that make everyday living more comfortable and secure.
For instance, underground parking provides vehicle safety and shields them from weather conditions, which is particularly important in a tropical climate.
A concierge service offers assistance with household matters, leisure arrangements, and general upkeep of the complex.
Amenities such as swimming pools, co-working spaces, fitness centers, and relaxation zones make apartments more desirable on the rental market.
High Rental Demand and Stable Income Bali’s popularity among tourists and expats remains consistently high, and apartments on the island attract renters year-round.
Digital nomads, tourists, and expats increasingly choose compact and functional apartments.
For property owners, this translates into steady income and high occupancy rates even during the low season.
Low Maintenance Costs Apartments incur lower maintenance costs compared to villas and townhouses.
The management company handles landscaping, cleaning, technical maintenance, and security.
This frees owners from extra hassles and ensures the property remains in good condition.
Additionally, saving on maintenance does not reduce the property's appeal, as renters receive all necessary amenities and services without needing to maintain them themselves.
High Liquidity and Growth Prospects The liquidity of apartments in Bali's real estate market allows investors to manage assets flexibly and quickly sell the property if needed.
Smaller size, more affordable price, and high demand make apartments attractive for resale, providing an opportunity to increase capital as prices rise.
As Canggu and other popular areas in Bali continue to develop, the value of apartments grows each year.
Ease of Transaction and Minimal Legal Risks In Bali, restrictions on full land ownership for foreign nationals can complicate the purchase of villas or townhouses.
With apartments, the process is much simpler: they can be purchased through a long-term leasehold, which doesn’t require complex legal structures.
This simplifies the purchase procedure and reduces risks associated with owning property in a foreign country.
Conclusion Apartments in Bali combine affordability, comfort, and the potential for successful investment.
Freedom from property maintenance, minimal concerns about wildlife, underground parking, and concierge service make them ideal for living and renting.
These benefits allow investors to enjoy a stable income while preserving the asset’s liquidity and value.

In this article, we look at how much apartments and villas cost, what factors affect their prices, and how property values vary across different areas of the island.

What Determines Prices Of Property in Bali The same budget can give buyers access to very different types of property in Bali, from compact apartments near the ocean to more spacious properties in less tourist-oriented areas.
That is why several factors should be considered when comparing options.
The main factors that influence the price are: location and distance from the beach; property type and size; stage of construction; leasehold term; project quality and infrastructure.
Location and Proximity to the Beach Location is especially important for buyers who plan to buy property in Bali and rent it out.
Properties in Canggu, Berawa, Seminyak, and Uluwatu usually cost more because these areas are in high demand among tourists and investors.
Proximity to the ocean and urban infrastructure also affects the price.
Property Type How much property in Bali costs largely depends on the type of property.
Studios, apartments, and villas fall into different price segments.
The price is influenced by the size, number of bedrooms, layout, private pool or terrace, as well as the features of the complex itself.
Stage of Construction Property in Bali includes both completed properties and projects at different stages of construction.
Prices are often lower at an early stage than after the project is completed.
At the same time, it is important to assess the developer’s experience, stated completion dates, and previously delivered projects.
Leasehold Term The decision to buy property in Bali on a leasehold basis requires careful consideration of the contract term.
The longer the remaining leasehold period, the longer the buyer has the right to use the property, which also affects its value.
Project Level The infrastructure of the complex also affects property price.
A swimming pool, fitness area, spa, workspace, restaurant, parking, and security increase the cost of developing and maintaining the project and may place it in a higher price segment.
How Much Does Property in Bali Cost in 2026?
There is no single market price for property in Bali: the cost depends on the property type, size, location, and stage of construction.
In 2026, prices start at around $100,000 for compact apartments, while villas generally require a larger budget.
Apartment Prices in Bali in 2026 How much does property in Bali cost?
At the more affordable end of the market, apartment prices in Bali in 2026 start at around $100,000 for compact units and selected properties at the construction stage.
One-bedroom apartments are most commonly priced between $120,000 and $200,000, while larger two-bedroom units may cost from $180,000–200,000 and above.
Premium apartments are usually more expensive due to their larger size, amenities provided, complex infrastructure, and location.
Prices for such properties can cost more than $300,000.
How Much Does a Villa in Bali Cost?
A villa in Bali represents a separate price segment.
According to industry data, the median price of villas on the island is approximately $256,000–299,000.

Depending on the property class: smaller villas may cost less than the median price; two- or three-bedroom villas with more space and a private plot often cost $300,000–600,000 or more; premium properties can cost over $500,000, while large high-end villas may reach $1 million or more.
Property Prices in Different Areas of Bali One of the key features of the market for property in Bali is the noticeable difference in prices across different parts of the island.
In some areas, prices are supported by stable tourist demand, while in others the main factors are limited land availability or proximity to the ocean.
Canggu and Berawa High rental demand is one of the reasons why many investors choose to buy property in Bali specifically in Canggu and Berawa.
These areas already have well-developed infrastructure for living and leisure, including restaurants, beach clubs, international schools, and fitness centres.
This supports demand for both short-term and long-term rentals.
Uluwatu Uluwatu clearly shows how much real estate prices can depend on the exact location.
The terrain of the peninsula varies considerably, so land with ocean views or convenient access to popular beaches can cost significantly more than plots farther inland in Bukit.
Seminyak A villa in Bali in an established tourist area such as Seminyak can be more expensive because of dense development and the limited availability of vacant land.
At the same time, well-developed tourism infrastructure helps maintain stable demand for property in the area.
Other Areas of Bali Buyers who are willing to buy an apartment or a villa in Bali outside the main tourist centres have a wider range of options.
Pererenan is developing alongside neighbouring Canggu, while Ubud is more focused on quiet stays, long-term living, and wellness tourism.
In less developed areas, prices may be lower, but tourism infrastructure is usually more limited.
How Property Prices in Bali Are Changing in 2026 Overall market trends are also affecting apartment prices in Bali in 2026.
According to industry analysis, prices have increased by around 7% over the past year, although the pace of growth varies significantly depending on the quality and location of the project.
At the same time, supply is increasing.
Around 4,260 new residential units are expected to be completed on the island in 2026, increasing competition between projects.
Buyers are paying closer attention to: construction quality; the infrastructure and amenities of the complex; location; property management terms.
Demand is also supported by strong tourist arrivals.
In April 2026 alone, Bali welcomed more than 553,000 international visitors.
This continues to support interest in properties designed for both short-term and long-term rentals.
Conclusion For buyers, property in Bali in 2026 offers a wide range of options with differences in price and features.
The final budget depends on the area, property type, stage of construction, and leasehold term.
The choice of developer in Bali is equally important: their experience, the quality of completed projects, and ability to meet deadlines directly affect the reliability of the purchase.
Compact apartments remain the most affordable option, while villas and premium properties require a significantly larger budget.
Growing supply is giving buyers more choice and making the market more competitive.
When comparing properties, it is therefore important to consider the project’s features, location, and potential for future rental income.

How to Buy Real Estate in Bali as a Foreigner What Foreigners Need to Know in 2026 to Buy Real Estate in Bali Interest in Bali real estate remains strong, but so does the number of questions from international buyers.
Today, people are looking beyond the price of a villa, flat, or off-plan apartments in Bali.
They also want to understand how the purchase process works, which ownership options are available to foreigners, and what costs to expect before and after signing the contract.
If you plan to buy real estate in Bali as a foreigner, it is important to know that the legal framework differs significantly from many European countries.
Foreigners can legally purchase property in Bali, but they cannot own land under freehold title in their own name.

Before choosing a property, it is worth understanding: whether foreigners can buy property in Bali and which ownership structures are available; how the transaction works from selecting a property to completing the legal documentation; the total cost of purchasing property, including additional fees; which property taxes should be taken into account; which legal documents should be verified before paying a deposit.
In 2026, the key question is no longer simply which villa to choose.
It is how to structure the transaction in a transparent, secure way that matches your investment goals.
Can Foreigners Buy Property in Bali?
One of the first questions buyers ask is whether a foreigner can purchase a villa or apartment in Bali and register it in their own name.
The short answer is yes, but Bali real estate for foreigners is subject to specific legal restrictions and ownership rules.
Foreigners cannot obtain Hak Milik, the Indonesian freehold title available only to Indonesian citizens.
This is why the common phrase "buying a villa in Bali" is not the same as owning land under Indonesian law.
Foreign buyers can use the property, invest in it, rent it out, or transfer their rights, but only within the legal ownership structures available to them.

In practice, foreigners can buy property in Bali through several legal options: Leasehold — a long-term lease of land or property; Hak Pakai — the right to use a property; PT PMA — acquiring eligible property rights and conducting commercial activities through a foreign-owned company registered in Indonesia.
The right option depends on your investment goals.
One ownership structure may be suitable for a private residence, another for a rental business, and another for long-term investment or resale.
That is why, before signing a purchase agreement, it is essential to evaluate not only the property, location, and price but also the legal rights you will receive after the transaction is completed.

Bali Real Estate for Foreigners: Available Ownership Options For foreign buyers, purchasing property in Bali is typically based on either a legal right to use the property or ownership through a specific legal structure.
The option you choose determines how long you can hold the property, whether you can rent it out, and the conditions for selling or transferring your rights in the future.
It is important to distinguish between the three main ownership structures: Leasehold, Hak Pakai, and PT PMA.
These are not different versions of the same purchase method but separate legal mechanisms with different rights, timeframes, restrictions, and purposes.
Leasehold: Long-Term Lease Leasehold is one of the most common options in Bali real estate for foreigners.
In practice, it is a long-term lease of land or a property rather than freehold ownership.
There is no standard lease term for every transaction.
While agreements of 25–30 years are common, the exact duration is negotiated between the parties and specified in the contract.
This option is suitable for buyers who plan to use the property as a private residence, a holiday home, or a rental investment.
However, the lease agreement itself is the most important document in the transaction.

Before signing, make sure to review: the lease term; extension conditions; the cost of extending the lease; whether the lease rights can be transferred to another buyer; restrictions on the use of the property; what happens to the building when the lease expires; the responsibilities of each party.
Leasehold can be a practical ownership structure, but its security depends largely on the quality of the contract and proper legal due diligence.
Hak Pakai: Registered Right of Use Hak Pakai is a registered right to use property in Indonesia.
It may be available to foreign buyers who meet specific legal requirements, including holding the appropriate immigration documents and having a valid legal status in Indonesia.
Hak Pakai is generally intended for buyers who want to use the property primarily as their private residence or for personal purposes.
It is important to understand that the right to use a property does not automatically grant the right to operate it as a short-term rental or commercial investment.
If your goal is to rent out a villa, this should be verified before completing the purchase with a qualified lawyer, notary, or licensed property consultant in Indonesia.
They should review the property's legal documentation, land zoning, permitted land use, ownership registration, and whether the required licenses for rental activities can be obtained.
Otherwise, you may discover that the property is perfectly suitable for private use but cannot legally be rented to tourists.
Hak Pakai may provide stronger legal protection than a standard lease agreement.
However, if your objective is Bali real estate investment or generating rental income, this ownership structure should be evaluated carefully.
In many cases, another legal structure, such as PT PMA, may be more appropriate.
PT PMA: Buying Property Through a Company PT PMA is an Indonesian company with foreign ownership.
Through this legal entity, foreign investors can acquire eligible property rights and conduct commercial activities in Indonesia.
For those planning to buy real estate in Bali as a foreigner, PT PMA is not a way to "buy a villa in your own name." It is a business structure designed for commercial operations.
This option may be suitable if you plan to rent out the property, manage rental income, or hold it as an investment asset.
It is important to understand that establishing a PT PMA does not grant a foreigner Hak Milik (freehold ownership of land).
This title is available only to Indonesian citizens.
A PT PMA can hold only those property rights that are permitted under Indonesian law.
For a rental business, registering a PT PMA alone is not enough.
It is also essential to verify the company's business activities, required licenses, land zoning, permits, and whether the property rights have been structured correctly.

What to Choose: Apartment, Villa, or Townhouse in Bali?
Bali offers a wide range of property types, including apartments, villas, and townhouses.
Each option has its own advantages and suits different investment goals.
To help you decide what to look for when you buy property in Bali, let’s explore the pros and cons of each type.
Apartments: Convenience and Lower Maintenance Apartments are an excellent option for investors seeking stable rental income.
Apartments are an excellent option for investors seeking stable rental income.
They are compact, easy to rent long-term, and particularly popular in well-developed areas such as Canggu.
Professional property management companies manage most apartments, so owners do not need to handle day-to-day maintenance themselves.
This helps reduce ongoing ownership and maintenance costs.
Villas: More Space and Privacy Villas are highly sought after by travellers who value privacy, space, and comfort.
Many feature private swimming pools and landscaped gardens, making them especially attractive for the short-term rental market.
However, villas generally require higher maintenance costs than apartments due to their larger size and the upkeep of outdoor areas, pools, and gardens.
Townhouses: A Balance Between Convenience and Privacy Townhouses combine many of the advantages of apartments and villas.
They typically offer more living space, multiple floors, and greater privacy while requiring less maintenance than a villa.
They suit tenants looking for more space and privacy than an apartment can provide, without the additional maintenance responsibilities that come with a villa.
Which Property Type Is Right for You?
The right choice depends on your investment objectives.
Apartments are ideal for investors looking to minimise maintenance costs while generating consistent rental income.
Villas may be a better fit for those willing to invest more in property upkeep in exchange for strong potential in the short-term rental market.
Townhouses offer a practical middle ground for investors seeking a balance between space, privacy, and maintenance costs.

Why is Bali Real Estate Increasing in Value?
Just a few years ago, buying property in Bali was mainly seen as an investment in holiday real estate.
Today, the market has evolved.
New residential developments continue to emerge across the island, infrastructure is expanding, and demand remains strong throughout the year, well beyond the peak tourist season.
What is driving property prices upward?
Let's look at the key factors.
Consistently strong rental demand One of the main reasons Bali property prices continue to rise is the island's strong rental market.
Throughout the year, Bali attracts tourists, entrepreneurs, families, and remote professionals from around the world.
Many of them are looking for more than a hotel room.
They prefer apartments or villas where they can stay for several weeks or even months.
This keeps both short-term and long-term rental demand high, particularly in Canggu, Pererenan, Seminyak, Ubud, and the Bukit Peninsula.
Limited supply of land Land available for development in Bali's most desirable locations is limited.
Plots close to the ocean, established amenities, and convenient transport routes are especially sought after.
As more land is developed, the number of available plots continues to shrink, pushing land prices higher.
This has a direct impact on the value of newly built villas and apartments.
Why location matters Even within the same area, property prices can vary significantly.

The value of a property depends on factors such as: distance from the beach; road access; nearby restaurants, shops, and fitness facilities; future development potential of the area; the level of competition among rental properties.
That is why properties in the best locations within the same neighbourhood often appreciate faster than those in less convenient areas.
Higher standards in new developments Today's buyers pay closer attention to architecture, layouts, interior finishes, and professional property management.
As a result, modern developments increasingly offer a wider range of on-site facilities and services.
New developments in Bali may include swimming pools, fitness centres, yoga studios, restaurants, lounge areas, and professional property management.
These projects require larger investments to develop, but they are better aligned with the expectations of international buyers and tenants.
As a result, they tend to remain more attractive for both rental income and future resale.
Growing interest from international investors Many investors view Bali real estate as an opportunity to generate rental income while benefiting from long-term capital appreciation.

The strongest demand is typically focused on projects that offer: prime tourist locations; professional property management; a clear and transparent legal structure; well-developed infrastructure; a realistic investment model.
Strong international demand also helps support property values across the market.
Which properties are more likely to appreciate?
Owning property in Bali alone does not guarantee future price growth.

The investment potential of a property depends on several factors working together, including: the popularity of the location; construction quality; property management standards; ongoing maintenance costs; rental demand; the level of competition from nearby properties.

A villa or apartment within a thoughtfully designed residential development may offer better long-term value than a larger standalone property with poor access, limited infrastructure, and no professional management.
Is buying property in Bali worth considering?
The Bali real estate market continues to grow, supported by strong tourism, limited land availability, and an increasing number of high-quality residential developments.
However, any purchase decision should be based on careful due diligence.
It is important to assess the location, legal documentation, ownership structure, the developer's reputation, maintenance costs, and expected rental returns.

Investment Guide in Bali for Beginners Investing in Bali real estate can be an attractive option for first-time buyers.
Consistent rental demand, ongoing infrastructure development, and the island’s popularity among tourists support interest in local property, particularly apartments.
Those planning to buy property in Bali should first understand the local market and the rules involved in completing a purchase.
This guide covers the main steps and key considerations involved in investing in Bali real estate.
Why invest in Bali real estate?
Bali benefits from steady rental demand due to its popularity among tourists and expats.
Areas such as Canggu offer a combination of leisure, developed infrastructure, and comfortable living, attracting both short-term visitors and long-term tenants.
Apartments can perform well across both rental markets, giving owners greater flexibility and access to a broader tenant base.
How to choose the right investment property?
When selecting a property in Bali, consider its price, rental demand, location, and potential for capital appreciation.
Apartments in popular areas such as Canggu often attract consistent interest from tenants and may be easier to resell than some other property types.
Developments with facilities such as swimming pools, co-working spaces, security, and underground parking can be more attractive to tenants and support stronger rental performance.
What returns can investors expect?
Rental returns depend on the location, property class, occupancy rate, seasonality, and quality of management.
Some apartment projects advertise rental yields of 10–15% per year, with potentially higher figures in the premium segment.
However, actual returns should be calculated after accounting for management fees, taxes, maintenance costs, and periods without tenants.
Buying an apartment during the construction stage may also provide an opportunity for capital appreciation once the project is completed.
Some developments project value growth of up to 20–30%, but these figures are not guaranteed and should be assessed against comparable properties and current market conditions.
What property ownership options are available in Bali?
One of the most common options for foreign investors is leasehold ownership, which grants the right to use a property for a period specified in the agreement.
Leasehold properties may be used personally or rented out, depending on the terms of the contract.
Before proceeding with a purchase, investors should check the remaining lease term, extension conditions, transfer rights, and permitted use of the property.
All documents should be reviewed by an independent local legal adviser.
What are the main maintenance costs?
Apartments are generally easier and more cost-efficient to manage than standalone villas.
In many developments, a property management company handles cleaning, repairs, security, and the upkeep of shared facilities such as swimming pools and common areas.
Owners may also need to cover utilities, management fees, routine maintenance, and contributions toward the operation of the development.
The total cost depends on the size of the apartment, the level of service, and the facilities available, so all regular fees should be confirmed before purchasing.
Taxes and legal considerations Taxes and transaction costs depend on the legal structure of the purchase, the ownership format, the property’s status, and the way rental income is received.
Expenses may include taxes related to the purchase or sale, tax on rental income, notary fees, and other administrative charges.
Before completing a transaction, investors should consult a local legal and tax specialist.
They can confirm the applicable rates, review the ownership structure, and calculate the full cost of purchasing and holding the property.
How can investors reduce risks?
To reduce risks, it is important to work with an established developer and an independent legal adviser.
Investors should verify the land documents, construction permits, contractual terms, project timeline, and the developer’s track record.
It is also worth assessing actual rental demand, competition in the area, management costs, and future infrastructure plans.
A popular location can support demand, but it does not guarantee a particular return or increase in property value.
How liquid is Bali real estate?
Apartments in popular areas, including Canggu, may attract interest on the resale market due to developed infrastructure and rental demand.
However, the time required to sell a property depends on its price, condition, location, remaining lease term, management quality, and current market conditions.
A well-positioned property can give investors more flexibility and may be easier to resell when necessary.
Before purchasing, it is useful to review comparable resale listings and understand how long similar properties typically remain on the market.
How to get started with property investment Begin by defining your budget, investment goals, preferred location, and property type.
Compare several projects, review their management terms, calculate all expected costs, and carry out an independent legal check before signing any agreement.
Apartments in Canggu may suit first-time investors due to the area’s popularity, developed infrastructure, and wide range of available projects.
Each property should still be assessed individually based on its financial projections, legal status, and market position.

Apartments in Bali: The Best Choice for Investment When it comes to real estate in Bali, investors often find themselves torn between purchasing a villa, townhouse, or apartment.
However, when analyzing the advantages of each type of property, it becomes clear that apartments have unique features that make them more attractive to modern investors and renters.
Affordable Entry Cost and Low Investment Threshold Apartments in Bali offer a relatively low entry threshold into the real estate market.
This allows investors to acquire property with lower costs compared to villas or townhouses, leaving room for high potential returns.
Investors looking to minimize purchase and maintenance expenses will find apartments to be an optimal choice.
Minimal Maintenance and Clean Living Space One key aspect that sets apartments apart from villas and townhouses in Bali is the absence of certain “wildlife” that may appear in private yards.
Since apartments lack large open spaces, owners don’t have to worry about unwanted “neighbors” like snakes, geckos, frogs, and other animals common to greener and more open areas.
Investors and renters who prefer a clean environment will find apartments much more comfortable for living.
Convenient Underground Parking and Access to Modern Amenities Modern apartment complexes in Bali offer essential amenities that make everyday living more comfortable and secure.
For instance, underground parking provides vehicle safety and shields them from weather conditions, which is particularly important in a tropical climate.
A concierge service offers assistance with household matters, leisure arrangements, and general upkeep of the complex.
Amenities such as swimming pools, co-working spaces, fitness centers, and relaxation zones make apartments more desirable on the rental market.
High Rental Demand and Stable Income Bali’s popularity among tourists and expats remains consistently high, and apartments on the island attract renters year-round.
Digital nomads, tourists, and expats increasingly choose compact and functional apartments.
For property owners, this translates into steady income and high occupancy rates even during the low season.
Low Maintenance Costs Apartments incur lower maintenance costs compared to villas and townhouses.
The management company handles landscaping, cleaning, technical maintenance, and security.
This frees owners from extra hassles and ensures the property remains in good condition.
Additionally, saving on maintenance does not reduce the property's appeal, as renters receive all necessary amenities and services without needing to maintain them themselves.
High Liquidity and Growth Prospects The liquidity of apartments in Bali's real estate market allows investors to manage assets flexibly and quickly sell the property if needed.
Smaller size, more affordable price, and high demand make apartments attractive for resale, providing an opportunity to increase capital as prices rise.
As Canggu and other popular areas in Bali continue to develop, the value of apartments grows each year.
Ease of Transaction and Minimal Legal Risks In Bali, restrictions on full land ownership for foreign nationals can complicate the purchase of villas or townhouses.
With apartments, the process is much simpler: they can be purchased through a long-term leasehold, which doesn’t require complex legal structures.
This simplifies the purchase procedure and reduces risks associated with owning property in a foreign country.
Conclusion Apartments in Bali combine affordability, comfort, and the potential for successful investment.
Freedom from property maintenance, minimal concerns about wildlife, underground parking, and concierge service make them ideal for living and renting.
These benefits allow investors to enjoy a stable income while preserving the asset’s liquidity and value.

La zona ofrece una combinación perfecta de tranquilidad y accesibilidad, ideal para quienes buscan un estilo de vida relajado junto a la costa.
La ubicación de Grand Bay permite disfrutar de una gran variedad de playas con muy poca densidad de turistas.

Playas cercanas como Sabinillas, Alcaidesa o la emblemática Cala Sardina destacan por su belleza natural y sus espectaculares vistas, ofreciendo vistas panorámicas al Peñón de Gibraltar y la costa norte de África.
Cala Sardina, en particular, es la primera playa mediterránea de la provincia de Cádiz, sin edificaciones alrededor, ofreciendo un entorno exclusivo para disfrutar del sol y el mar.

La zona es ideal para los amantes del golf, ya que cuenta en sus proximidades con campos de prestigio como Valderrama, Sotogrande, San Roque Club, La Cañada y La Duquesa, todos a pocos minutos en coche.
Además, los campos de polo de Sotogrande, cercanos a Grand Bay, acogen cada año importantes torneos internacionales, ofreciendo una experiencia única para los aficionados a este deporte.

Para quienes buscan ocio náutico, a pocos kilómetros se encuentran dos puertos deportivos: el de La Duquesa, con embarcaciones de recreo y pesqueros, y el exclusivo puerto de Sotogrande, con yates de lujo, tiendas, bares, restaurantes y cafeterías.
Ambos puertos son un referente de la vida marítima de la Costa del Sol y ofrecen un ambiente animado durante todo el año.
Manilva combina naturaleza, mar y deporte, proporcionando un estilo de vida mediterráneo auténtico.

Vivir en Grand Bay significa disfrutar de un entorno privilegiado, con playas casi vírgenes, campos de golf de primer nivel y todos los servicios necesarios a mano, desde restaurantes hasta conexiones de transporte y zonas de ocio.
Gibraltar, y su aeropuerto internacional, está a 35 Kilómetros de la promoción (menos de 1 hora en coche).
En Gibraltar se puede disfrutar de una amplia oferta comercial y gastronómica internacional, así como de interesantes puntos de interés turístico.

CINCO PRIORIDADES QUE CONSIDERAR PARA INVERTIR La Riviera Maya es uno de los destinos internacionales con mayor desarrollo inmobiliario; en particular, Playa Del Carmen es una ciudad que presenta enormes oportunidades de inversión para quienes buscan invertir su patrimonio en una residencia vacacional.

A continuación, le presentamos cinco prioridades que le sugerimos tomar en cuenta al momento de decidir invertir su patrimonio: PATRIMONIO Asegúrese de invertir en desarrollos con un modelo de negocio que le garanticen plusvalía de largo plazo.
Preste especial atención a la reputación del administrador y evalúe el tiempo que se compromete a estar al frente del desarrollo.
Es importante conocer el alcance del desarrollo y los proyectos de mediano y largo plazo que se plantean para la propiedad en que desea invertir.
DISFRUTE Considere el esquema de amenidades y servicios que le ofrece el desarrollo.
Una segunda residencia en la playa implica altos costes de mantenimiento, pago de impuestos y distintas gestiones que deberá tomar en cuenta.
Busque esquemas de inversión que le permitan disfrutar de su propiedad en el Caribe sin tener que preocuparse por la administración de su residencia.
INVERSIÓN INMEJORABLE Invertir en bienes raíces es un asunto de rentabilidad.

En el caso de las residencias vacacionales, el valor de su inversión se mide en dos vertientes: el ahorro que implica tener una propiedad con servicios y amenidades y la rentabilidad que genera su propiedad al arrendarse.
Cerciórese de invertir en un modelo de negocio que sea transparente en su rendición de cuentas y que le garantice los mejores dividendos.
CONFIANZA ¿En manos de quién está poniendo su patrimonio?
Investigue la historia y experiencia del desarrollador con el que planea invertir.
¿Qué otros proyectos ha operado y de qué forma lo ha hecho?
¿Qué dicen sus clientes sobre su modelo de negocio?
No escatime en hacer todas las preguntas que sean necesarias para obtener la certeza de que su dinero está en las mejores manos.
CERTEZA JURÍDICA Busque proyectos que le ofrezcan certeza jurídica, transparencia y rendición de cuentas.

Foto: MORROS VITA - API El desarrollo inmobiliario en la zona norte de Cartagena suma un nuevo capítulo con el inicio de morros Vita, el más reciente proyecto sobre la línea de playa en el macroproyecto Serena del Mar.

La iniciativa, liderada por Epic Diseño + Construcción en asocio con Novus Civitas, marca el cierre de una etapa de expansión residencial en este sector del Caribe colombiano, consolidado como uno de los polos de inversión más dinámicos de la ciudad.
Morros Vita es el último de los proyectos en primera línea de playa dentro del complejo morros, una familia de desarrollos que ha venido transformando el paisaje urbano de la zona.

Su ubicación privilegiada, frente a las playas de Manzanillo del Mar, ofrece una conexión directa con el entorno natural, uno de los principales atributos que buscan los compradores de este tipo de desarrollos.

Durante este periodo, se espera la generación de aproximadamente 700 empleos, entre directos e indirectos, vinculando mano de obra y empresas contratistas principalmente de Cartagena y Barranquilla.
Este impacto laboral refuerza el papel del sector constructor como motor de la economía regional.
Desde el punto de vista arquitectónico, el proyecto apuesta por un diseño inspirado en la biofilia, una tendencia que busca integrar la naturaleza con los espacios habitables.
Según sus promotores, la propuesta se traduce en formas orgánicas, estructuras curvilíneas y el uso de materiales que favorecen la conexión con el entorno.
La idea central gira en torno a un concepto de “lujo apacible” , entendido como bienestar, equilibrio y calidad de vida.

La industria del libro resiste a la era digital y se fortalece en Colombia Morros Vita se suma a una trayectoria consolidada dentro del complejo, donde Epic Diseño + Construcción ya ha desarrollado cerca de 1.300 apartamentos en ocho proyectos, entre ellos Eco, Ío, Zoe, Eos, Kai, Aura y Park I.
Este último se encuentra próximo a ser entregado en 2026, mientras que Aura avanza en su construcción con fecha estimada para 2027.
Además, recientemente se anunció el lanzamiento de morros Park II, evidenciando la continuidad de la apuesta inmobiliaria en la zona.
Uno de los componentes más relevantes del desarrollo urbanístico es la creación de un gran parque central, denominado “Central Park Verde Azul” , que conectará varios de los proyectos residenciales.
Este espacio será diseñado por Arquitectónica GEO, una firma especializada en paisajismo y sostenibilidad.
La propuesta busca integrar áreas verdes, espacios de recreación y recorridos peatonales, aportando valor ambiental y social al conjunto.
A esto se suma la proyección de un centro comercial dentro del área de morros, que tendrá entre 20 y 30 locales comerciales.
Este espacio incluirá servicios esenciales como bancos, droguerías y minimercados, pensados para atender las necesidades cotidianas de los residentes.
Su apertura está prevista para finales de 2027, consolidando así una oferta integral que combina vivienda, comercio y entorno natural.

En este lote, en los límites de Medellín e Itagüí, Acierto Inmobiliario ofreció dos proyectos: Flora y San José Natura.
Ambos terminaron abandonados y con pocos avances.

FOTO: CORTESÍA DUMED ABOGADOS Santiago Olivares Tobón Metro Publicado 30 de julio de 2026 Actualizado 30 de julio de 2026 bookmark Guardar Los afectados del proyecto Reserva Natural San José Natura, obra abandonada desde diciembre de 2022 en Itagüí, Antioquia, tienen una esperanza de recuperar el dinero invertido.
Todo porque la Superintendencia Financiera condenó a Alianza Fiduciaria, fiducia de este proyecto, a pagarle a uno de los centenares de afectados de esta obra de la constructora Acierto Inmobiliario.

Esta sentencia podría marcar la hoja de ruta de, al menos, 50 personas que interpusieron acciones legales en contra de la fiducia y la constructora para que les respondan por el dinero invertido en este proyecto, que debía ser culminado en 2023 y no hay avance de obra en una obra de 629 apartamentos.

El afectado recibirá 67 millones de pesos, producto del dinero invertido como parte de la cuota inicial del proyecto, además de la indexación por el tiempo que el dinero estuvo en poder de esta fiducia, que respaldó este proyecto que era No Vis (No Vivienda de Interés Social).

El abogado Jhon Jairo Morales, representante de la firma Dumed Abogados, que llevó a cabo este proceso por parte de los afectados, aseguró que “logramos demostrar que Alianza Fiduciaria incumplió los deberes de información, diligencia y protección que le impone la ley como profesional especializado del sector fiduciario”.

Entérese: Acción Fiduciaria tendrá que pagarle $85 millones a una familia por proyecto de vivienda fallido en Bello Agregó el abogado que “además, quedó acreditado que continuó realizando desembolsos de recursos cuando el proyecto ya se encontraba paralizado”.

Uno de los inconvenientes de esta obra de Acierto Inmobiliario, que tiene más de 100 proyectos con conflictos en todo el Valle de Aburrá y el Oriente antioqueño, es que se utilizó el mismo lote para dos obras, ya que en la misma zona se encuentra Flora, un proyecto VIS que también se encuentra paralizado y tiene un avance de menos del 50%.

Le puede interesar: Así es la odisea de arrendar vivienda en Medellín, la ciudad de Colombia donde ‘cuesta un ojo de la cara’ La sentencia por parte de la Superintendencia Financiera se logró luego de que se recopilaran pruebas, documentos y se hiciera una práctica de interrogatorios para tener las evidencias suficientes para que se lograra condenar a esta fiduciaria por las anomalías en otro proyecto fracasado.

Entre los aspectos que tuvo en cuenta esta superintendencia para la decisión se encontró que había falta de información en la etapa precontractual, la omisión en la entrega de documentos esenciales por parte de la fiducia y la constructora y la ausencia de información sobre el estado del proyecto.

Además, se pudo comprobar que quienes estaban a cargo de la obra desde el tema financiero no cumplieron con la verificación para la entrega de recursos y hubo inconsistencias sobre la estructuración del proyecto y se le entregaron recursos a la constructora después de la parálisis de la obra en diciembre de 2022.

Desde la firma de abogados no solo se espera que en próximos días haya sentencias similares relacionadas con San José Natura, sino con los demás proyectos de esta constructora que han dejado a miles de familias con el sueño frustrado de tener un hogar nuevo.

Preguntas frecuentes 1.
¿Por qué la Superintendencia Financiera condenó a Alianza Fiduciaria por el proyecto San José Natura?

La Superintendencia Financiera concluyó que Alianza Fiduciaria incumplió sus deberes de información, diligencia y protección frente a uno de los compradores del proyecto Reserva Natural San José Natura.
Además, determinó que realizó desembolsos de recursos cuando la obra ya se encontraba paralizada.
¿Cuánto dinero deberá devolver Alianza Fiduciaria a uno de los compradores afectados?

La decisión ordena el pago de 67 millones de pesos , correspondientes al dinero entregado como cuota inicial, más la indexación por el tiempo que esos recursos permanecieron bajo administración de la fiduciaria.
