The project brings together refined architecture, thoughtful spatial planning, and direct access to the waterfront — creating a living environment that balances privacy with a strong sense of place.

Designed for residents who value both comfort and aesthetics, Canal Bay reflects a contemporary residential vision shaped by its island setting, where natural light, open water, and clean architectural lines define everyday life.

Prime Location: Lusail, Qetaifan Islands Qetaifan Island North is one of the most distinctive addresses in Lusail City — a master-planned destination that has become the centerpiece of Qatar's urban expansion.
Canal Bay occupies a privileged position on this island, placing residents just steps from the water's edge.
The location offers a rare combination: the energy and infrastructure of a growing modern city alongside the calm and visual breadth of island life.
Surrounded by canals, open sky, and carefully planned public spaces, the setting gives Canal Bay a character that is difficult to replicate elsewhere in the region.
Connectivity and Accessibility to Key Locations Despite its island setting, Canal Bay is well-connected to the wider Lusail and Doha network.
Residents benefit from proximity to major roads and transport links that make daily commuting and leisure travel convenient.

Direct access to Lusail City's main road network via Qetaifan Island bridges Short drive to Lusail Boulevard, one of Qatar's premier commercial and dining destinations Close proximity to Lusail Stadium and the Lusail Marina District Easily accessible from central Doha via the Lusail Expressway Nearby public transport infrastructure connecting residents to broader Qatar Transit Network routes Property Types and Sizes Canal Bay offers a selection of residential units crafted to suit a range of lifestyles, from individuals and couples to families seeking generous living spaces.
Each unit has been designed with an emphasis on natural light, ventilation, and views toward the surrounding waterfront and landscaped areas.

Residential apartments across multiple configurations to accommodate diverse household needs Units designed to maximize exposure to natural light and outdoor scenery Thoughtful interior layouts that balance open-plan living with defined private spaces Detailed Amenities and Facilities Canal Bay provides residents with a focused set of amenities that support an active, comfortable, and secure lifestyle without unnecessary excess.
Every facility has been selected with daily liveability in mind.

Shared gym equipped for fitness and wellness routines Indoor swimming pool offering year-round access regardless of weather conditions Private beach access giving residents a direct connection to the island's waterfront Landscaped parks and green areas designed for relaxation, recreation, and outdoor gathering CCTV security systems operating throughout the compound for continuous residential safety Unique Architectural Features and Design Elements The architecture of Canal Bay draws from the island's natural qualities — water, light, and open horizon — and translates them into a built form that feels both purposeful and visually cohesive.
The exterior combines glass panels, brushed aluminum, and natural stone, creating facades that respond to changing light conditions throughout the day.

Rather than imposing itself on its surroundings, the project's massing and orientation were considered carefully to preserve sightlines and allow waterfront scenery to remain central to the residential experience.
The result is a development that feels grounded in its location while maintaining a clean, contemporary identity.
Lifestyle and Community Aspects Living at Canal Bay means becoming part of one of Qatar's most dynamic and thoughtfully developed communities.
Qetaifan Island North is designed as a walkable, mixed-use environment where residential life, leisure, retail, and waterfront access coexist naturally.
Residents of Canal Bay enjoy not only the compound's own amenities but also the broader island ecosystem developing around them.

Walkable access to waterfront promenades and open public spaces on the island A growing community of professionals, families, and expatriates drawn to Lusail's urban offer Proximity to leisure, dining, and entertainment venues within the Lusail City masterplan A quiet residential atmosphere that contrasts with — yet remains connected to — the activity of central Lusail Investment Potential and Market Value Qetaifan Island and Lusail City represent one of the most compelling real estate investment stories in the Gulf region.
As Qatar continues its sustained economic and infrastructure development, demand for quality residential property in planned urban destinations like Lusail has shown consistent strength.
Canal Bay's waterfront address, reputable developer backing, and position within a fully serviced island community contribute to its long-term value proposition.

For investors, the combination of a desirable location, limited island supply, and growing rental demand from Qatar's professional and expatriate population makes Canal Bay a credible addition to a real estate portfolio.
For owner-occupiers, it offers a rare opportunity to own a home with genuine waterfront character in one of the region's most carefully developed cities.
Developer Profile: TAAMEER Development TAAMEER Development is a real estate developer with a track record in delivering residential and mixed-use projects across key growth markets in the region.
The company approaches development with an emphasis on quality of construction, design integrity, and creating environments that retain their appeal over time.

Canal Bay represents TAAMEER's commitment to bringing well-conceived, properly executed residential projects to high-demand locations — combining sound investment fundamentals with a genuine focus on how people live day to day.

Their presence on Qetaifan Island reflects confidence in the long-term trajectory of Lusail as a destination, and a willingness to build developments that contribute positively to the communities forming around them.

Dar Global's debut Saudi project, freehold, from £609,000, completing December 2027.
Picture a wide, three-storey villa that opens onto its own garden, on a walkable street a few doors from the school, the mosque and the park your children will grow up with.

That is the life Neptune Interiors by Mouawad is built for: not a home stranded on a plot, but a home inside Sedra, the whole community that ROSHN, the Public Investment Fund's national housing developer, is building in north Riyadh.

Neptune is a gated address of 200 five-bedroom villas, each about 300 to 420 square metres across three floors, and it is the debut Saudi project of Dar Global, the London-listed development arm of Dar Al Arkan.
The interiors carry the name of Mouawad, the high-jewellery maison, in what is described as its first move into real estate.
Dar Global develops the villas and carries delivery; Mouawad provides the interior design; ROSHN masters the Sedra community around them.
What makes Neptune a place to live, rather than simply a villa to own, is Sedra itself.
This is not a subdivision with a gate and a name.

It is a planned neighbourhood designed so that daily life happens close to home: its own schools and early-childhood centres, mosques, health-care clinics, parks and green corridors, sports facilities, retail and dining, a community centre, and walkable streets that connect them.

Sedra sits in northern Riyadh, east of Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University, with the Wadi Hanifah green corridor running through the wider area, and within easy reach of the capital's business and diplomatic districts.

King Khalid International Airport is about 15 minutes away, the King Abdullah Financial District about 19 minutes, and the city centre about 26 minutes, so a family is settled inside a self-contained community yet minutes from the parts of Riyadh that matter.
The project is under construction now, with completion targeted for December 2027.
The handover date quoted at the September 2024 launch has already moved out, so treat the target as a target, not a guarantee.

In detail A closer reading.
Neptune's real setting is Sedra, and it is worth knowing the community before the villa.

Sedra is ROSHN's flagship residential community in north Riyadh, being built out across several phases east of Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University, with the Wadi Hanifah green corridor in the wider landscape.

ROSHN, the Public Investment Fund's national housing developer, has planned it as an integrated neighbourhood, so schools, early-childhood centres, clinics, mosques, parks, sports facilities and retail sit inside the community rather than a drive away, along walkable streets and green space.
From the community, King Khalid International Airport is about 15 minutes by car and Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University about 10 to 11 minutes.
The King Abdullah Financial District is about 19 minutes, King Fahd Stadium about 17 minutes, and central Riyadh about 26 minutes.
This is what a genuinely planned Riyadh neighbourhood looks like, and Neptune is a freehold home inside it.
Neptune is a single, considered product within Sedra: 200 detached villas, each five bedrooms across three storeys, of about 300 to 420 square metres of built-up area.
The structure is worth understanding before you buy.
Dar Global is the developer and carries delivery.

Mouawad, the high-jewellery maison, licenses the interior design only, under the line 'Interiors by Mouawad', in what is described as its first move into real estate; it is a design and brand partner, not the builder.
ROSHN is the master-developer of the Sedra community in which the villas sit, not the developer of Neptune itself.
So three names attach to the address, but responsibility for building and handing over your villa rests with Dar Global.
Dar Global is the international development arm of Saudi Arabia's Dar Al Arkan.
It was established in 2017 and listed on the London Stock Exchange in February 2023 under the ticker DAR.
Its usual model is branded residences aimed at overseas buyers, and its home activity has been in the Gulf and abroad rather than inside the Kingdom, which makes Neptune its debut Saudi project.

That is the honest delivery picture: a listed developer with a track record of branded schemes, taking on its first project on home soil, partnering a jewellery house that is itself new to real estate.
We do not quote Dar Global's self-reported portfolio totals as fact, and we encourage buyers to weigh the debut nature of the project alongside the developer's listing and parentage.

The residences are uniform in type and generous in size: every villa is a five-bedroom, three-storey freehold home of about 300 to 420 square metres of built-up area, designed for families who want room to spread across distinct floors.
Per-villa features described for the scheme include private gardens, terraces or roof gardens, EV charging, and maid, staff and driver rooms together with a majlis.
The interior design is licensed from Mouawad.

Because the homes are a single five-bedroom type, the choice between villas is about position and floor configuration within the community rather than a wide spread of layouts; the published built-up range is 300 to 420 square metres.
On demand and investment, here is the honest picture with the counterweights left in.
Neptune's draw is a large detached villa inside a Public-Investment-Fund-backed community, close to the airport and the financial district, in a capital seeing heavy investment in housing.

Against that, the project is under construction with a completion target that has already slipped once, the developer has not published a fixed from-price, and the building developer is taking on its first Saudi scheme.
The 23 June 2026 geographical-zones approval names Sedra, but the specific Neptune property and title conditions must still be checked against the live REGA record.

New Developments New Developments News News Sign up Location Company Development Name News QLD Aniko Group breaks ground on $2.5 billion The Landmark in Mermaid Beach Aniko Group breaks ground on $2.5 billion The Landmark in Mermaid Beach Joel Robinson Jun 12, 2025 CONSTRUCTION UPDATE Local Gold Coast developer Aniko Group has officially launched the first stage of The Landmark, a $2.5 billion masterplanned, mixed-use development in Mermaid Beach .
With construction now underway, the project marks one of the most ambitious and transformative undertakings in Queensland’s recent history.
The Landmark will comprise four towers with a mix of apartments, premium commercial space, fine dining, and a 5-star internationally branded hotel.
The first stage of the project will complete in 2027, through Aniko 's own construction arm, Aniko Constructions.
240 apartments are part of the first release.
George Mastrocostas, Founder and Managing Director of Aniko Group, said the project has been years in the making.
"[It] embodies our long-held aspiration to create something truly exceptional,” Mastrocostas said.

“To simultaneously launch and begin construction on The Landmark represents more than just a milestone; it’s a clear and confident statement about our intent and capability." “Having our in-house construction team build The Landmark allows us to maintain oversight across every detail and progress with absolute confidence, even as the broader industry faces significant headwinds.” Located on the corner of Seaview Avenue, the site places residents within walking distance of Pacific Fair, The Star Casino, and the bustling precincts of Broadbeach and Mermaid Beach .

Created in collaboration with acclaimed design firm Plus Architecture , the residences feature spacious two- and three-bedroom layouts, many with dedicated study nooks, designed to capture panoramic views of the coastline, hinterland, and cityscape.
A suite of amenities will be available exclusively to residents, including a lagoon pool, pickleball court, golf simulator, arcade, Pilates studio, spa, sauna, and a state-of-the-art gym.
“We’ve imagined The Landmark as far more than a place to live, it’s a lifestyle precinct that brings together community, wellness, entertainment, and world-class design,” Mastrocostas added.
“We’re proud to contribute something of enduring value to the Gold Coast .
This development will generate jobs, elevate expectations, and enrich the urban fabric of our city.
It’s a privilege to play a role in shaping that future.” Construction of stage one is now underway.

A localização, próxima do Miradouro de Nossa Senhora do Monte e de alguns dos locais mais emblemáticos da cidade das sete colinas – como o Castelo de São Jorge ou o Panteão Nacional –, e a vista sobre o casario Lisboeta e o lado Sul do Tejo, tornam a experiência de viver no coração de um dos bairros históricos em algo único e exclusivo.
Aqui, pode desfrutar do lado mais tradicional de Lisboa numa casa que prima pela qualidade – dos materiais, dos acabamentos e dos equipamentos.

O edifício, com a assinatura ARX Portugal Arquitetos – a mesma equipa do emblemático Castilho 203 que venceu vários prémios do sector – e o design de interiores de Gracinha Viterbo , tem tudo para se tornar numa referência urbana.

Estes dois elegantes edifícios reinterpretam a tradição lisboeta com cores suaves, pedra e azulejo.

Ler mais O edifício residencial, situado no alto da Rua Damasceno Monteiro, imediatamente abaixo do miradouro da Nossa Senhora do Monte, do qual se desfrutam as mais deslumbrantes vistas da cidade, tem tudo para se tornar em mais uma referência urbana.
Debruçado sobre a cidade, no bairro histórico da Graça, de onde segundo a tradição se respiram os melhores ares de Lisboa.
Localizados perto de Alfama, estes apartamentos com vista para o rio em Lisboa são a escolha perfeita para aqueles que procuram desfrutar do melhor que esta cidade tem para oferecer.

Do Castelo de São Jorge, à ilharga e o imenso casario da baixa aos pés com o rio e a margem sul ao fundo, compõem um cenário majestoso que faz deste edifício uma homenagem à arte de viver a cidade das sete colinas.

Desenvolvido numa linguagem arquitetónica contemporânea, com a assinatura do gabinete ARX Portugal Arquitectos, o Terraços do Monte privilegia naturalmente das amplas varandas e vidraças que, tornam literalmente cada apartamento num miradouro privado alcandorado na encosta da Colina de Santo André.

E se é de beleza que falamos quando falamos deste edifício, a arte, de que a Vanguard Porpeties faz uma das suas bandeiras, não poderia deixar de estar presente através de uma obra site specific criada por um artista português.

Overview Overview Plans + Pricing How to Buy Image gallery FAQs Share URL copied to clipboard 8 Pratt Street The Kubrick Named for Stanley Kubrick, the visionary filmmaker who reshaped modern cinema, The Kubrick carries that same spirit of precision, detail and daring use of colour.
This luminous new landmark set in the leafy heart of Freemans Bay comprises 52 apartments over nine levels in two-, three- and four-bedroom configurations.
There’s an extraordinary range of floorplans and many have ‘A’, ‘B’ and even ‘C’ options.
The homes at The Kubrick range from 60-280sqm and enjoy enhanced access to light and cross-flow ventilation due to the building’s serene internal courtyard with a Japanese-inspired garden.

For those seeking an extraordinary urban home, there are four sub-penthouses – all with generous 3-metre ceilings, expansive outdoor living and sweeping views – and an entire floor penthouse so dramatic, it should probably have its own agent.
At Ockham, we believe shared spaces carry weight because life needs room to breathe.
For The Kubrick we have dedicated over 600sqm to best-in-class common facilities.
There’s a residents’ lounge with gourmet kitchen, a drinks suite, an outdoor covered pool, a 120sqm gym with sauna and ice bath and an office with bookable boardroom.
There are also 85 carparks with EV charging and generous storage options.

Dr Galia Barhava explains why she bought at The Kubrick The development site is unique, bordered only by the gorgeous Harry Dansey Reserve to the north and west, the Freemans Bay Community Centre, Anglesea Street, and Pratt Street, offering a sense of privacy and connection to nature unusual in an inner-city suburb.
It is a leafy oasis, yet everything that defines Auckland’s most vibrant inner suburbs lies at your doorstep.

The bustling restaurants, bars and shops of Ponsonby Road, Karangahape Road, and the city are just minutes away, along with some of the city’s best-loved public spaces, such as Western Park and Victoria Park.
The Kubrick is a rare flower in the heart of the city – a place of artistry and amenity.
Considered shared spaces At Ockham, we believe shared spaces carry weight because life needs room to breathe.
For The Kubrick we have dedicated 616m² of space that will ensure onsite activities well into next century.
Come on a tour To find the perfect pastel bricks for The Kubrick, Ockham returned to the Sant’Anselmo brick company from Veneto, Italy.
Beautiful bricks Founded by the De Checchi family in Loreggia, Northern Italy – not far from Venice – Sant’Anselmo’s kilns have been firing bricks for five generations.
Today, Sant’Anselmo exports globally.
Read more The vision behind The Kubrick Rooms with a point of view The interiors of The Kubrick draw inspiration from the extraordinary range of hydrangea hues.
While the exterior glows with light-catching, opalescent bricks in the flower’s brighter tones, the palette subtly deepens as you step inside, shifting toward the richer, warmer shades of the flower.

1428 Brickell Continues Ascent Into Miami’s Brickell Skyline Credit: The Boundary for Ytech.

By: Oscar Nunez 8:00 am on September 3, 2026 Construction continues to advance at The Residences at 1428 Brickell, an 861-foot-tall residential skyscraper rising at 1428 Brickell Avenue in Miami’s Brickell neighborhood.

Developed by Ytech and designed by Arquitectonica, with interior architecture and design by ACPV ARCHITECTS Antonio Citterio Patricia Viel, the 70-story tower will contain 195 condominium residences and more than 80,000 square feet of private amenity space.
Coastal Construction is leading construction, with Capform handling concrete work, and completion is anticipated in late 2028.
In a recent LinkedIn post , Ytech reported that 1428 Brickell is now reaching Level 25 as vertical construction continues above Brickell Avenue.

Credit: Ytech Recent construction photos featured on the project’s official website show the reinforced concrete superstructure extending well above the podium, with perimeter formwork, vertical reinforcing steel, and wall forms advancing around the active deck.
A concrete placing boom is positioned across the upper levels as crews continue the floor-by-floor concrete cycle.

Two tower cranes positioned outside the building footprint continue to service the structure, contrasting with the apparent internally positioned crane rising through Santander Tower across Brickell Avenue at 1401 Brickell Avenue.

The tower’s sculptural profile is also becoming increasingly pronounced, with rounded corners, curving slab edges, and wave-like elevations giving physical form to the voluptuous proportions depicted in the renderings.
The tower’s floor plates also appear relatively repetitive across most of the structure, which should support a fairly consistent formwork cycle as vertical construction continues.

The primary variation occurs along the Brickell Avenue elevation, where the slab edges shift in and out to form the building’s wave-like profile, while the remaining elevations are considerably more uniform and largely flush from floor to floor.
Credit: Ytech Several floors below, façade installation is progressing across the residential levels, with portions of the panel system still covered in protective blue film.

A closer look at the emerging envelope suggests that the tower will feature relatively little opaque wall area across these levels, relying instead on exposed structural columns and broad expanses of floor-to-ceiling glass.
The resulting column-and-glass composition should maximize natural light and outward views within the residences, a treatment commonly associated with ultra-luxury condominium design.
Credit: Ytech Taking a closer look at the parking podium, its substantial concrete massing currently forms a largely blank base beneath the residential tower.
Renderings indicate that at least two of the visible elevations will eventually be treated with vertically oriented, ribbed paneling, introducing a strong vertical expression across the podium.
That treatment will contrast sharply with the horizontal balcony bands, rounded slab edges, and wave-like curves defining the residential volume above.

Credit: Ytech Credit: Ytech Credit: Ytech The latest progress follows the completion of the tower’s mat foundation in September 2025, when approximately 13,000 cubic yards of concrete were placed during a continuous 33-hour operation.
The pour incorporated roughly 2,700 tons of reinforcing steel and required more than 1,300 concrete truck deliveries, establishing the base for vertical construction.
The west-facing elevation will incorporate the project’s Solar Backbone, a system of approximately 500 photovoltaic-integrated windows spanning nearly 20,000 square feet.
The glazing is designed to generate up to approximately 175,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity annually for use within the building’s common areas.
The Residences at 1428 Brickell will contain 195 condominium residences ranging from two to four bedrooms, along with more than 80,000 square feet of private amenity space.
Planned amenities include multiple swimming pools, fitness and wellness facilities, private dining and entertainment areas, guest suites, and resident spaces near the upper levels.
Ytech secured $565 million in construction financing for the project in November 2025 from J.P.
Morgan and Sculptor Real Estate, with JLL Capital Markets arranging the financing.

Lucia Times Business Arts & Culture Lifestyle Read ePaper Search Read Latest ePaper Tuesday, November 3, 2026 READ LATEST EPAPER Search Local News Court Crime Economy Editorial Education Politics Tourism Weather Sports Athletics Basketball Cricket Football Horse Racing Olympics Business Energy Budget Technology Tourism Arts & Culture Bajan Vibes Crop Over Entertainment Lifestyle Regional Lifestyle Travel Food & Drink Home & Garden Health & Wellness Shopping Work Magazines Listen Capital Media HD Cita Radio 90.1 FM Careers © 2024 All Rights Reserved Home » Posts » Pendry Barbados marks milestone as luxury resort nears completion Business Local News Tourism Pendry Barbados marks milestone as luxury resort nears completion by Ricardo Roberts 22/04/2026 written by Ricardo Roberts Updated by Benson Joseph 22/04/2026 3 min read A+ A- Reset A view of the construction of the exterior of the Pendry Residences in St Peter Facebook Twitter Linkedin Whatsapp Email 3.3K B arbados’ north-west coast has gained the region’s first Pendry-branded resort in all but name, after developers topped off the US luxury hotel and residences group’s maiden international project on Wednesday — a 2027-bound scheme built by Canada’s largest listed contractor.

The event marks the completion of the primary structural phase for the luxury hotel and residential development, which is set to become a landmark international destination for the California-based brand.
The ceremony, attended by Prime Minister Mia Mottley and other government officials, served as a formal introduction of the Pendry brand to the Caribbean.

Michael Fuerstman, co-founder of Pendry Hotels & Resorts, noted that while the company has projects worldwide, this particular development had captured global attention: “I travel around the world meeting clients and partners, and everybody wants to know about Barbados,” Fuerstman said.
“This is the one destination that creates the most excitement.
It’s aspirational, it’s exciting, and it’s a great lifestyle.” For the Fuerstman family, the project carries a deep personal resonance.
Alan J.
Fuerstman, founder, chairman and chief executive of Montage International, shared a story of visiting the island in 1985 to escape the rigours of raising toddlers — including his son Michael.

He emphasised that the resort is designed to harmonise with the natural environment, noting: “Imagine just hearing the surf.
You just open the windows and it’s so compelling.
Our guests will hear that a little over a year from now.” The project is being built by Aecon Construction Group, Canada’s largest publicly traded construction firm.
Marty Harris, executive lead and senior vice-president of Aecon, highlighted the technical precision required to bring the vision to life.
“Luxury begins long before a guest arrives,” Harris said.

“It begins in the foundations, the structures, and the details that will never be seen but will always be felt.” He also noted that the project had prioritised local talent, having already onboarded graduates from the Barbados Construction Gateway Training Initiative and launched community support programmes such as “From Our Home to Yours”.
Upon its scheduled completion in 2027, Pendry Barbados will feature approximately 80 oceanfront guest rooms and 46 luxury residences.
The sprawling site will include a 110-berth marina, the Pendry Yacht Club, a signature spa and several dining experiences.
Michael Fuerstman described the architectural result as “spectacular”, noting the unique combination of a marina, jungle and residential living emerging from the sea.
“I don’t know that there’s another hotel residential development like this in the world,” he added.

The questions serious investors actually ask.
Straight answers — no hype.
Can foreigners own property in Indonesia?
Not freehold.
Foreign investors typically use a long-term leasehold (25–30 years) with a contractually agreed renewal, or a properly structured PT PMA company.
We arrange everything through a licensed notary and show you the full chain of title before you commit.
Are the yields guaranteed?
No — and be wary of anyone who says they are.
We publish an estimated yield range — an estimate, not a forecast.

The figures beside it (nightly rate, occupancy, costs) are the inputs to the calculator above, so you can model your own investment amount; they are not how the published range was derived, so your result will differ from it.
That range is modelled on a different investment basis — ask us for it in writing before you commit.
Property values and rental income can go down as well as up.
What happens at the end of the leasehold?
Your agreement includes a pre-negotiated renewal option at defined terms.
We walk you through the renewal mechanics and the exit scenarios (resale of the remaining lease) up front, in writing.
Who manages the property and how do I get paid?
Our island-based team handles listings, guests, maintenance and reporting.
You receive net income with itemised monthly statements — you always see gross revenue, costs, and your payout.
What are the real risks?
Regulatory change, construction delay, occupancy shortfall, currency movement, and liquidity (leasehold resale takes time).
We underwrite conservatively and disclose each risk per project.

Can you please briefly describe the process and timing of purchasing my property?

Are there any restrictions in buying a residential property in The Ellinikon that arise from my country of origin?
No, there are no restrictions in buying a residential property in The Ellinikon associated to the purchaser’s country of origin.
Can I buy a property as an individual, or is it possible to purchase it through a legal entity?
Purchasers are free to choose how they wish to purchase their property, either as individuals or via a Greek or foreign legal entity.

The Purchaser can sign the Reservation Agreement either as individual or legal entity, in which case, the Sale & Purchase Agreement should be signed by the same physical/legal entity, or parent, child or spouse or a legal entity where the entity that signed the RA holds more than 50%.
Do I pay VAT when I purchase a residential property in The Ellinikon?
No, all purchases of residential properties in The Ellinikon are exempted from VAT until the 31/12/2026.
Can I apply for a Golden Visa when purchasing a property in The Ellinikon?
Yes, the buyer of a property in The Ellinikon can apply for a Golden Visa, according to the current legislation, where the minimum value of the property is €800,000.

Adjacent to the affluent neighbourhoods of Bangsar, Sri Hartamas and Bukit Tunku, the enclave is set to see the development of yet another luxurious condominium.
The second and final phase of the RM9 billion Pavilion Damansara Heights will have two residential towers named Imperial Residences and Royal Suites, as well as a hotel/corporate office tower.
Together, they have a total gross development value of about RM2.5 billion and are currently open for private preview.

Pavilion Group project director Joey Ung says this new phase, spanning 6.08 acres, is designed based on feedback from buyers who are looking for larger units in a fully integrated environment, which is something very rare in this area.
“There are a number of improvements.
Phase 1 was designed more than eight years ago.
We gathered buyer feedback to improve the ID (interior design), workability and functionality.
For example, in Phase 1, we used compressed marble.
For Imperial Residences, we chose natural marble to bring out luxury and elegance.
We are going back to a classic way to meet buyer expectations.
It still has the consistent Pavilion DNA but with a more contemporary, elegant trend,” she explains.
“Also, we have dual-key layouts in Royal Suites, which we didn’t have in the previous phase.
We realised that young families or families with teenagers want more privacy than just a standard room.
Not many luxury residences offer dual-key, but we listened to buyer feedback.

The response has been promising.” Ung: By thoughtfully combining residential living with commercial spaces, we are creating more than just homes; we are shaping a complete lifestyle destination [at Pavilion Damansara Heights] (Photo by Zahid Izzani/The Edge) The 9.27-acre Phase 1, comprising Windsor Suites, Regent Suites and Crown Residences (residential) as well as nine corporate towers, was launched in 2017 and is largely completed.
The 57-storey Windsor Suites has 568 units, with the typical unit sizes ranging from 614 to 1,831 sq ft and two penthouses of 6,483 sq ft.
Meanwhile, the 57-storey Regent Suites has 581 units of 605 to 1,878 sq ft and two penthouses of 6,612 sq ft.
Crown Residences offers bigger units of 2,303 and 2,803 sq ft and a penthouse of 10,058 sq ft.
There are a total of 165 units in this 50-storey tower.
About 99% is taken up across its residential towers, while the corporate suites are fully sold.
The towers sit atop the Pavilion Damansara Heights mall, which is also connected to the Pavilion Damansara Heights MRT Station.

The show unit of Imperial Residences (Photo by Zahid Izzani/The Edge) New phase Meanwhile, in the latest phase, the 50-storey Imperial Residences will have 148 luxury homes with built-ups of 3,380 and 4,090 sq ft and six penthouses of 7,459 sq ft.
It was designed based on feedback from buyers looking for larger units and modelled after Crown Residences.

Its features include a private lift lobby, natural marble in the living room, clear demarcation of public and private spaces for absolute privacy, bespoke facilities such as a spa, therapy room, club lounge and fully equipped function room as well as Pavilion Concierge services.

“Imperial Residences’ design approach attracts owner-occupiers in the surrounding affluent neighbourhoods such as Damansara Heights, Bangsar, TTDI (Taman Tun Dr Ismail) and Bukit Tunku as well as downsizers from other places who still prefer larger units at Malaysia’s most affluent address,” Ung notes.
“The design and concepts will also draw parallels with other affluent neighbourhoods around major cities in the world.

We also target global citizens, both Malaysians and foreigners, who maintain properties around the world and choose to stay in a place that offers lifestyle amenities in just one city.” Prices range from RM5.07 million to RM10.2 million, or an average of RM2,000 psf.
The 51-storey Royal Suites will have 490 residential units measuring 452 to 1,679 sq ft.
It will offer a new product range, which includes studio and dual-key units.
Ung says the dual-key layout, which is not available in Phase 1, accounts for 33% (163 units) of the tower.
Also, the development departs from conventional layouts by excluding standard one-bedroom units.
Instead, it offers “compact” studio units and larger “1+1” configurations, reflecting a more functional approach to space planning.
The size range appeals to both investors and owner-occupiers.
Ung explains that Royal Suites’ unit sizes are designed to attract both groups, with its strongest selling point being its proximity to the MRT station.
She notes that connectivity is especially important for investors, and being the closest tower to the MRT gives it a clear edge in rental demand and long-term value.
She adds that larger units are positioned on higher floors to maximise views of the Kuala Lumpur skyline, and that floor zoning has been planned to enable price differentiation within the tower.
These units will be priced from RM700,000 to RM4.2 million, or an average of RM2,000 psf.
The 31-storey hotel/corporate suites tower, scheduled for completion in 2H2027, will have 135 strata corporate suites, with built-ups from 1,152 to 2,852 sq ft, on Levels 15 to 31.
Some 75% have been sold, at an average price of RM1,700 psf.
The hotel suites will occupy Levels 7 to 13.

The facilities at Regent Suites include a function room and gymnasium (Photo by Pavilion Group) Legacy address Ung believes the new phase can further enhance Pavilion Damansara Height’s appeal as a vibrant, fully integrated ecosystem.
“The expanded components introduce a larger, more dynamic community, creating greater vibrancy and a stronger sense of place.

With more office workers and residents working and living within the development, the retail mall will benefit from increased footfall and sustained activity throughout the day and evening, supporting a wider variety of curated retail, dining and lifestyle offerings.
This, in turn, elevates the overall living experience, making daily conveniences even more accessible and enjoyable,” she says.
She adds that, together with the existing nine corporate towers and three residential towers, the expansion will enhance the development’s critical mass and maturity.

In addition, seamless connectivity via the mall unifies all components, providing sheltered and convenient access across residential, corporate and retail spaces, while promoting efficiency, encouraging social interaction and reinforcing its position as a self-sustaining urban hub, Ung says.
Crucially, the entire development is directly connected to the Pavilion Damansara Heights MRT station, anchoring it within Kuala Lumpur’s expanding rail network.

“The seamless connectivity to the MRT [Kajang Line], combined with the retail, office and residential components, allows us to create a complete ecosystem where people can live, work and socialise in one place,” says Ung.
“An integrated development like Pavilion Damansara Heights is designed with a long-term vision in mind.
By thoughtfully combining residential living with commercial spaces, we are creating more than just homes; we are shaping a complete lifestyle destination.

A place where convenience, community and opportunity come together in one destination.” The swimming pool at Crown Residences (Photo by Pavilion Group) ESG as a baseline Another critical layer underpinning the development is its ESG (environmental, social and governance) framework.
Both residential towers in the new phase are designed in accordance with Singapore’s Building and Construction Authority Green Mark sustainability system.

Ung notes that it is done through a range of energy-efficient, water-saving and environmentally responsible features, such as high-performance glazing to reduce heat gain, centralised chiller systems for efficient cooling and LED lighting that delivers at least 40% energy savings compared to conventional systems.

She says the façade incorporates high-performance glazing, achieving a Residential Envelope Thermal Value of 18.86 W/m² — outperforming the 25 W/m² baseline under Singapore Standard 530:2006 — while a centralised chiller plant operates at 0.7 kW/RT for energy-efficient cooling.

She adds that energy use is further reduced through LED and T5 lighting, which deliver at least 40% savings over conventional incandescent systems, alongside Variable Voltage Variable Frequency motors and sleep mode in lifts to optimise performance, while the basement car park is mechanically ventilated to improve air circulation.

Ung says water efficiency is addressed through certified fittings integrated into a building management system for real-time monitoring, while low-VOC (volatile organic compound) materials enhance indoor environmental quality.
At the urban level, the development’s direct MRT connectivity, supported by covered walkways, encourages public transport usage and reduces reliance on private vehicles.
“This is about ensuring the development remains relevant and sustainable over the long term,” Ung says.

Façade of The Senique Hanoi project in the East of Hanoi.
Photo courtesy of the CapitaLand Development (CLD).
The complex, located on a prime site in the east of the capital city, has a projected total gross development value of over SDG600 million ($455.5 million).

This follows the successful launch of Lumi Hanoi ’s Phase 1 and Phase 2 in Tay Mo ward, Nam Tu Liem district in the west of Hanoi, during which over 3,100 units – about 97% of the more than 3,200 available units – were booked.
Facade of Lumi Hanoi project in the west of Hanoi.
Photo courtesy of CapitaLand Development (CLD).
The Senique Hanoi and Lumi Hanoi are part of CapitaLand Development’s plan to add 11,000 residential units in the next five years to 27,000 residential units in Vietnam by 2028.
Including these two residential projects, CLD’s portfolio in Vietnam now comprises over 18,000 quality homes across 18 developments.
For The Senique Hanoi, CLD collaborates with two esteemed capital partners – Mitsubishi Estate Co., Ltd.
and Nomura Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.
– both of whom are renowned developers from Japan.

"The Senique Hanoi will leverage the site’s prime location and excellent infrastructure to cater to homebuyers seeking a high-quality living environment and strong investment potential," said Alwin Low, general manager of North Vietnam of CLD (Vietnam).

"Together with our joint venture partners, Mitsubishi Estate and Nomura Real Estate, we look forward to enhancing the eastern part of Hanoi with this thoughtfully designed residential project, which aims to meet the aspirations of city dwellers for style, wellness and connectivity," he noted.
Spanning approximately 2.1 hectares, construction of The Senique Hanoi is slated to commence in Q3/2024 and scheduled for completion in 2027.
It enjoys convenient access via the Hanoi-Hai Phong Expressway, within a 30-minute drive from the Central Business District, and a 40-minute drive from the Noi Bai International Airport.
Its connectivity will be further enhanced with the upcoming Metro Line 1 and Metro Line 8.

The Senique Hanoi is also close to a range of attractive amenities in Ocean City, such as an artificial saltwater lagoon and a freshwater lake, green parks, themed attractions, international schools, VinUniversity, shopping malls, and medical centers.
The project will feature about 2,150 units across three 37-storey towers, to be developed in two phases.
Homebuyers can choose from a wide array of unit types, ranging from one-bedroom units starting at 42 square metres to four-bedroom units measuring up to 186 sqm.
The development will also include duplex units and penthouses ranging from 118 sqm to 430 sqm.
On the positive market reception to Lumi Hanoi, Low added that Lumi Hanoi marks a significant milestone in CapitaLand’s 30-year journey in Vietnam.

It offers top-tier facilities, thoughtful design, functional layouts and ample parking, all in line with the company's goal of enhancing homeowners’ lifestyles by blending luxury, convenience and wellness into their everyday lives.
"We are heartened that Lumi Hanoi has gotten off to a good start, attracting strong demand for its first two phases.
Riding on the positive momentum, we are preparing to hold an exclusive preview of Lumi Hanoi’s Phase 3 in Q4/2024.

"In line with CapitaLand Development’s commitment to supporting Vietnam’s sustainable urbanisation journey, we continue to seek long-term investment opportunities, focusing on residential and commercial sectors," Low stated.

In addition to Lumi Hanoi, CLD achieved healthy results during the exclusive previews of Sycamore in Binh Duong New City in the southern province of Binh Duong, successfully selling over 70% of The Orchard, the development’s first gated community residence.
CLD is also making good progress with the construction of its projects.
The 173-unit Heritage West Lake, CLD’s first luxury residential development in Hanoi, will begin handing over to homeowners in September 2024.
CapitaLand Development (CLD) boasts a portfolio worth SDG21.3 billion ($16.16 billion) as of 30 June 2024.

Its well-established real estate development capabilities span across various asset classes, including integrated developments, retail, office, lodging, residential, business parks, industrial, logistics and data centers.
CLD (Vietnam) oversees and grows CLD’s investment and development business in Vietnam, one of CLD’s core markets where it has built an extensive presence over 30 years.
CLD (Vietnam)’s portfolio comprises one SOHO development, two integrated developments, and over 18,000 quality homes across 18 residential developments.

5 days ago 3.0 3 out of 5 rating Abhi I’ve spent a fair amount of time around Business Bay and it’s one of those areas that looks exactly how you’d expect Dubai to look - sleek, central, and always a bit on the go.
Location-wise, it’s hard to fault.
You’re minutes from everything includes the likes of Downtown, DIFC, Sheikh Zayed Road, and almost next door to The Dubai Mall, which is obviously one of the biggest highlights of the city.
Getting around is pretty seamless overall, and public transport is a big plus here: metros, buses, and cabs are all easily available, so you’re not fully reliant on a car.
What’s interesting about Business Bay is that while it’s very work-driven, it’s also quite residential, so you get a mix of both.
There are loads of cafés, gyms, and restaurants, and the canal side is genuinely a highlight, especially in the cooler months when it’s great for a walk or even cycling.
That said, it can feel a little… transactional.
A lot of people are there for work, so it doesn’t always have that strong “community” vibe.
Traffic can also be a bit chaotic during peak hours, and depending on the building, quality really varies; some are great, others not so much.
Overall, it works really well if you want convenience, connectivity, and that polished city feel, with the added bonus of actually being able to live there and not just work there.

One-bedroom units measure between 765 and 913 sqft, starting from 2M AED, while two-bedroom apartments range from 1,100 to 1,367 sqft, priced from 2.9M AED.
Three-bedroom apartments are available from 1,641 to 2,202 sqft, with prices beginning at 5.2M AED.
Duplex options include two-bedroom layouts from 1,410 to 2,718 sqft, starting at 4.5M AED, and three-bedroom duplexes from 3,343 to 3,448 sqft, starting at 9.1M AED.
For premium living, penthouses offer three bedrooms at 4,741 sqft from 17M AED and four bedrooms ranging from 5,286 to 5,964 sqft from 19M AED.
The collection is completed by an exclusive five-bedroom villa with 18,330 sqft, providing the largest and most luxurious option within the development.
When is DWTN Residences's Delivery date?
The scheduled delivery date for DWTN Residences is December 2030 .
This timeline allows for the completion of its 110-floor structure and integration of over 75,000 square feet of world-class amenities.
Developed by Deyaar Leasing, the project is set to become one of Dubai’s tallest and most prestigious residential towers, offering luxury living in Business Bay.
The completion date aligns with the developer’s commitment to delivering premium-quality residences designed for modern urban lifestyles.
Investors and future residents can plan confidently, knowing the project has a clear and targeted handover schedule backed by a reputable developer.

100% SOLD 100% SOLD DALIA NOW SELLING Register interest Frequently Asked Questions What should I know about Dalia before choosing a home?
Dalia is Phase 7 of Masaar 3, Arada’s forested villa and townhouse community in Sharjah.
The useful buying question is not simply whether Dalia sits in a green master plan, but which layout best fits you.
Across Masaar 3, the product range runs from 2- to 4-bedroom townhouses and 4- to 5-bedroom villas.
Homes are designed around rear-facing living and dining areas opening to private gardens or terraces, with the wider community organised around a central green spine.
Which Dalia townhouse works best for a couple or smaller family?
The 2-bedroom townhouse is the most compact typology in the Dalia range: a middle unit with an approximately 1,539 sq ft plot and 1,920 sq ft NSA.
It includes a maid’s room with ensuite, a closed kitchen, separate laundry, two ensuite bedrooms and a private backyard.
A 70 sq ft upper-floor landing adds useful flexible space for a desk, reading area or small family zone.
For buyers looking for a more compact home without giving up service space or a garden connection, the 2-bedroom townhouse provides a practical starting point.
What do I gain by moving from a 2-bedroom to a 3-bedroom townhouse?
The upgrade is not only an extra bedroom.

The 3-bedroom middle layouts offer a larger 1,705 sq ft plot, compared with approximately 1,539 sq ft for the 2-bedroom townhouse, while the total built-up area across the home increases from 1,920 sq ft to approximately 2,245–2,285 sq ft.
The additional space creates more flexibility across the home.
The living and dining area remains garden-facing, while the more generous upper landing can be used for a desk, bookshelves or a small family area.
For a growing family, regular guests or buyers planning to stay in the home for longer, the 3-bedroom townhouse provides more room to adapt without moving into the largest townhouse category.
Is a 3-bedroom corner townhouse worth considering over a middle unit?
The main difference is the additional land and outdoor space that come with the corner layout.
While both 3-bedroom middle layouts sit on plots of approximately 1,705 sq ft, the 3-bedroom corner townhouse has a larger plot of approximately 2,320 sq ft.
Being positioned at the end of the row also allows the corner home to bring in natural light from two sides and provides a larger garden area.
One of the bedrooms, in addition to the master bedroom, also has its own balcony.
The master bedroom includes a walk-in wardrobe, ensuite bathroom and private balcony.

For buyers deciding between the two, the corner townhouse is less about gaining another room and more about gaining a larger plot, additional outdoor space and the advantages of an end-of-row position.
What is the practical difference between the 4-bedroom middle and corner townhouses?
The corner layout gives you substantially more space.
Its plot increases from approximately 1,705 sq ft for the 4-bedroom middle townhouse to approximately 2,650 sq ft, while the built-up area increases from around 2,557 sq ft to 3,319 sq ft.
The corner home also includes a dedicated home office and benefits from a larger side garden, additional outdoor space and natural light from more than one direction.
Depending on how you use the home, the office could provide useful flexibility as a study, work-from-home space or additional room.

For buyers comparing the two layouts, the corner townhouse is therefore not simply a different position within the row; it provides a considerably larger plot and built-up area, together with additional indoor and outdoor space.
Which Dalia homes are strongest for working from home?
The 4-bedroom corner townhouse and both 4-bedroom villa layouts include a dedicated office or study, providing a separate room that can be used as a permanent workspace.
In the smaller townhouse layouts, the upper-floor landing provides more flexible space that could accommodate a desk or occasional work area, depending on how the household chooses to use it.
For buyers specifically looking for a separate, dedicated workspace rather than adapting part of another area, the 4-bedroom corner townhouse and 4-bedroom villas provide that option.
How do the two 4-bedroom villa types differ?
The biggest differences are in size, layout and how the additional space is designed.
Villa Type 1 is a semi-detached home on a plot of approximately 3,244 sq ft, with a built-up area of 3,465 sq ft.
It includes a rooftop level with a terrace and connected multipurpose indoor space, as well as a dedicated study.
Villa Type 2 is a larger, detached L-shaped home, with an approximately 4,430 sq ft plot and 4,210 sq ft of built-up area.

It does not have the additional rooftop level; instead, the layout includes a private pool, a separate majlis or formal living room, an ensuite guest bedroom on the ground floor and a family living area upstairs.

For buyers comparing the two, Type 1 offers the additional flexibility of rooftop indoor and outdoor space, while Type 2 provides a larger home and plot with more dedicated spaces for guests, family living and entertaining.
Should I choose a 4-bedroom corner townhouse or a 4-bedroom villa?
The 4-bedroom corner townhouse already offers substantial space, with approximately 3,319 sq ft of built-up area on a 2,650 sq ft plot, as well as a dedicated home office and larger corner garden.
Moving to a 4-bedroom villa changes both the scale and organisation of the home.
Villa Type 1 adds a rooftop terrace and multipurpose room, while the larger detached Type 2 adds a pool, majlis, ground-floor guest suite and separate family living room.
For buyers comparing the options, the villa layouts introduce more dedicated spaces for guests, formal entertaining and everyday family life.
Which Dalia homes include a private pool and majlis?
The larger 4-bedroom Villa Type 2 includes both a private swimming pool and a dedicated majlis/formal living room at the front of the home, separated from the family living areas.
Both 5-bedroom villa typologies also include a swimming pool and majlis.
In the 5-bedroom Type 2, the majlis has its own dedicated bathroom.
These layouts are therefore the clearest fit for buyers who want formal guest entertaining without opening the private family zones of the house.
How do the layouts support privacy and everyday family life?
Across the Dalia homes, several layout choices help separate shared, private and service spaces.
Guest powder rooms are positioned close to the entrance, while living and dining areas generally sit towards the rear of the home, opening onto the garden.
Master bedrooms include their own dressing space and ensuite bathrooms, and maid’s rooms are provided from the 2-bedroom townhouse upwards.
The larger villas provide further separation between different areas of the home.
Some layouts include a separate majlis or formal living room alongside family living spaces, while the 5-bedroom villas include an ensuite guest bedroom on the ground floor.

Stretching across approximately 4,900 acres with 7.2 kilometers of pristine Mediterranean shoreline east of Marsa Matrouh, this large-scale integrated community is designed to redefine coastal living in North Africa.

Far beyond a typical residential compound, Alam Al Roum is conceived as a complete destination — where private villas, hospitality venues, marinas, and leisure facilities come together along one of Egypt's most breathtaking coastlines.
Prime Location: North Coast Positioned along Egypt's North Coast, Alam Al Roum benefits from one of the Mediterranean's most naturally gifted stretches of land.

The North Coast has long been Egypt's premier summer destination, celebrated for its crystal-clear turquoise waters, powdery white sand beaches, and refreshing sea breeze that makes it a welcome escape from the heat of the city.

The specific location east of Marsa Matrouh places Alam Al Roum in a relatively unspoiled coastal corridor, offering residents a sense of genuine tranquility without sacrificing access to essential services and attractions.
The sweeping sea views and Mediterranean climate create a living environment that feels like a permanent vacation.
Connectivity and Accessibility to Key Locations Alam Al Roum is designed with accessibility in mind, connecting residents to major urban centers and transport hubs along the North Coast corridor.

Located east of Marsa Matrouh, a key coastal city with an international airport offering seasonal and year-round flights Accessible via the Alexandria–Matrouh Desert Road, one of Egypt's primary coastal highways Within driving distance of Alexandria, Egypt's second-largest city and a major commercial and cultural hub Proximity to Marsa Matrouh city center provides easy access to shops, hospitals, and everyday services The broader North Coast region continues to see significant infrastructure investment, improving road networks and travel times from Cairo and other major cities Property Types and Sizes Alam Al Roum offers a carefully curated selection of expansive villas built to accommodate a range of family sizes and lifestyle preferences.
Each residence is designed to maximize space, natural light, and sea views.

5-Bedroom Villas ranging from 307 to 453 square meters — ideal for families seeking generous living space with room to grow 6-Bedroom Villas at 601 square meters — among the largest residential offerings on the North Coast, suited for those who value exceptional space and privacy Detailed Amenities and Facilities Residents of Alam Al Roum have access to a thoughtfully planned set of amenities that cater to comfort, security, and everyday enjoyment.

Dedicated security personnel ensuring a safe and controlled residential environment around the clock CCTV surveillance systems covering key areas throughout the development Swimming pools offering residents a refreshing retreat just steps from their front door Beautifully maintained landscaped gardens that enhance the natural coastal scenery and create serene outdoor spaces for relaxation Unique Architectural Features and Design Elements The architecture at Alam Al Roum draws inspiration from Mediterranean coastal traditions, blending clean lines, open layouts, and natural materials to create homes that feel both elegant and grounded in their surroundings.
Villas are designed to make the most of their coastal setting, with generous facades, wide terraces, and spatial planning that draws the outside in.
The overall aesthetic favors understated refinement over ostentation — homes that age gracefully and feel deeply connected to the landscape around them.
Lifestyle and Community Aspects Life at Alam Al Roum is shaped by the rhythms of the sea and the ease of a well-planned community.
The development's masterplan envisions a fully integrated lifestyle destination that goes well beyond residential living.

A planned yacht marina for sailing enthusiasts and those who wish to explore the Mediterranean coastline Golf courses set within the broader development, offering a leisurely and scenic recreational option Hotel and hospitality facilities within the community, welcoming guests and adding vibrancy to the destination Commercial and retail areas providing everyday conveniences without the need to leave the compound A strong community identity fostered by shared green spaces, pedestrian-friendly pathways, and thoughtfully designed gathering areas Investment Potential and Market Value Egypt's North Coast real estate market has demonstrated remarkable resilience and consistent demand growth over the past decade, driven by both domestic buyers and international interest.
Alam Al Roum, developed by one of the Gulf's most credible real estate names, carries a level of trust and prestige that translates directly into long-term asset value.
The sheer scale of the masterplan — spanning nearly 5,000 acres with a diverse mix of uses — creates a self-sustaining destination economy that supports property values well into the future.

For buyers looking at second homes, seasonal retreats, or income-generating assets through short-term rental demand during peak summer months, this development presents a compelling opportunity in one of Egypt's most sought-after coastal corridors.
Developer Profile: Qatari Diar Qatari Diar Real Estate Investment Company is one of the most recognized development firms in the Middle East, wholly owned by the Qatar Investment Authority.

With a portfolio spanning multiple continents and iconic projects across Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Arab world, Qatari Diar brings a level of financial strength, planning expertise, and design ambition rarely seen in the Egyptian market.
Their involvement in Alam Al Roum is a strong indicator of the project's long-term credibility and delivery standards.
Buyers can invest with confidence knowing that the developer behind this coastal vision has a proven track record of completing large-scale, mixed-use destinations to an exceptionally high standard.
Alam Al Roum masterplan As a part of the North Coast masterplan, Alam Al Roum is a large-scale coastal development by Qatari Diar, located east of Marsa Matrouh on Egypt's North Coast.

Its expansive Mediterranean frontage sets it apart as one of Egypt's most ambitiously scaled coastal developments, designed to offer residents and visitors a complete seaside lifestyle.

Alam Al Roum is scheduled for delivery in 2030.

Given the scale of the masterplan — spanning 4,900 acres with residential, hospitality, marina, and commercial components — the 2030 timeline reflects a phased approach to building a fully integrated coastal destination on Egypt's North Coast.
Is Alam Al Roum a good investment?
Alam Al Roum stands out as a serious long-term investment on Egypt's North Coast.

Developed by Qatari Diar, one of the most credible names in regional real estate, the project sits on 4,900 acres with direct access to 7.2 kilometers of Mediterranean coastline east of Marsa Matrouh — a corridor that has seen consistent demand growth.
The masterplan is built around genuine lifestyle infrastructure: a yacht marina, golf courses, hotels, retail hubs, and recreational facilities.
This mix of amenities supports both capital appreciation and rental income potential, making it relevant to buyers, investors, and second-home seekers alike.
Large-scale integrated destinations like this tend to retain value better than standalone developments because the surrounding infrastructure drives sustained demand over time.
Is Alam Al Roum Freehold or Leasehold?
Alam Al Roum is a freehold development, meaning buyers hold full ownership of their unit.
Who is the Owner of Alam Al Roum?
Alam Al Roum is developed by Qatari Diar, a real estate investment company established by Qatar Investment Authority.
With a track record of large-scale, mixed-use developments across multiple countries, Qatari Diar brings institutional-grade planning and execution to the North Coast of Egypt.
Their involvement signals a project built to international standards with long-term development commitment.
Where is Alam Al Roum Located?
Alam Al Roum is located on Egypt's North Coast, east of Marsa Matrouh, along the Mediterranean Sea.
What are the Housing Options of Alam Al Roum?
Alam Al Roum offers villa units designed to suit different household sizes and space requirements, with two main configurations available.
The five-bedroom villas range from 307 to 453 square meters, offering a practical layout for families who want generous living space without excess.
These units balance indoor comfort with the coastal setting, providing enough room for private living areas, bedrooms, and outdoor access.
The six-bedroom villas are built at 601 square meters, making them the largest available option within the development.
At this size, the units are suited for extended families or buyers who prioritize expansive interiors and greater privacy.

Both configurations sit within a masterplan that includes a yacht marina, golf courses, hotels, commercial zones, and recreational facilities, meaning residents have direct access to a full range of services and lifestyle amenities.

The villa sizes, combined with the 7.2-kilometer Mediterranean coastline and the scale of the surrounding development, position Alam Al Roum as a destination for buyers seeking a primary residence, vacation home, or long-term coastal investment on Egypt's North Coast.

Except for aquarium fishes, a maximum of one (1) pet is allowed per unit.
Dogs and other similar pets are limited to a maximum height of two (2) feet when full growth is achieved.
Large, dirty, dangerous and foul smelling animals are not allowed in the unit.
Fighting cock and other type of chicken are not allowed in the premises.
Species/Animals that are declared endangered by local and international laws and organizations cannot be considered as pets.
The Condominium Corporation has the discretion to prohibit the retention of any pet within any unit which is found to be dangerous or a nuisance to other residents, or is kept in inhumane conditions.
Can a buyer renovate a unit?
The buyer can renovate the interior of a unit after acceptance of the unit from HTLand.
Buyers are not allowed to alter any exterior walls of their unit.
The buyer shall not introduce any improvements, alterations or additions to their unit without prior written consent from the Condominium Corporation.
Alterations or improvements done without prior written consent shall be subject to dismantling and demolition.
Are units allowed for short-term lease?
Residential units will be allowed for a minimum of one (1) month lease.
For the safety and security of the residents, short-term lease is not allowed.
Basic Utilities At Mandani Bay Where will be the water source of Mandani Bay?
Water will be supplied by the Metro Cebu Water District (MCWD).
In fact, MCWD will build a new water facility with in the reclamation area to supply the water requirements of Mandani Bay as well as the future developments within the reclamation area.
Who will supply the electrical requirements of Mandani Bay?
The electrical power of Mandani Bay will be sourced thru the Visayan Electric Company (VECO).
VECO has committed to supply the electrical power requirement for the entire Mandani Bay development.
Who are the sources of the telecommunication, cable TV and internet facilities?
Philippine Long Distance Telephone Company (PLDT) will be the exclusive service provider for telephone, cable and internet lines.
PLDT will be providing fiber-optic lines for the above-mentioned services thru their project, PLDT Fibr.
Fibr is the future .of broadband currently being used by international telephone operators like Verizon (US), BT Infinity (UK), etc.
This is the most advanced broadband service in the country that connects to the home via fiber-optic lines.
Traditional broadband services are usually through legacy copper lines, or cable.
PLDT Fibr’s use of fiber-optic cables guarantees the fastest and most stable internet connection for you.
In case of electrical interruption, will there be emergency power wherein electrical and water supply will not be interrupted?
Each podium of Mandani Bay is equipped with a generator set.
The generator set is designed to power 100% all electrical requirements of the residential units and the common areas (including elevators).
The retail and parking areas also have 100% power back-up.
The towers are equipped with cistern and tanks which serves as water storage for residential and commercial use.
Property, Residential & Parking Unit Ownership What is the land tenure for the project?
The land tenure is perpetual ownership, subject to the rules and implementing guidelines of Republic Act No.
4726, otherwise known as the “Condominium Act.” Can a non-Filipino citizen own a condo unit?
Foreigners can own one (1) or more condo units and will be issued a CCT under their name as proof of ownership.
Foreigners can own a maximum of 40% of the total saleable area (in terms of square meters) of a particular tower.
What are the requirements to purchase a unit?
Payment of required reservation fees.
Payment can be made in cash, check or thru credit card (master card or visa).
All check payment should be made payable to HTLand, Inc.
Completed and signed reservation agreement, payment term sheet and customer information sheet.

One (1) government issued ID (driver’s license, passport, PRC ID, SSS, GSIS, voter’s ID, etc.) After clearance of payment of reservation fees and completion of above mentioned documents the unit will be officially reserved under the buyer’s name.
Who can own a parking unit?
The owner of a parking unit should also be an owner of a condominium unit.
When a residential unit is forfeited, its corresponding parking unit is automatically forfeited.
What type of vehicles are allowed in a parking unit?
Only passenger-type vehicles or vehicles for personal use will be allowed to park.
What is the proof of ownership of a condominium and parking unit?

With its year-round sunshine, safe environment, and expanding tourism industry, the country is drawing attention from international buyers.
Among all the islands, Sal and its vibrant town of Santa Maria stand out as the top hotspots for property investment.
Tourism as the Engine of Growth The steady growth of Cape Verde’s tourism industry is the main driver of the property market.
Each year, more international visitors arrive on the islands, creating strong demand for holiday accommodation, second homes, and rental investments.
This consistent flow of tourists has a direct impact on real estate: property values are rising, and demand is growing, especially in Sal, which serves as the country’s main entry point.

Why Sal and Santa Maria Lead the Market Sal has several advantages that make it the heart of Cape Verde’s real estate boom: International Airport : Amílcar Cabral International Airport offers direct flights from major European cities.
Tourism Capital : Santa Maria is the island’s tourism hub, famous for its long beaches, hotels, and lively atmosphere.
International Buyers : Many Europeans already own second homes in Santa Maria, creating a strong and established expat community.
These factors make Sal not only attractive but also one of the safest bets for foreign investors.

더피알 [파이낸셜뉴스] 11월 분양가 상한제 적용 아파트 5000가구 이상이 시장에 공급된다.
분양가 상한제는 아파트 등 공동주택 분양 시 정부 기준에 따라 산정한 분양가격 이하로만 판매하도록 하는 제도다.
3일 부동산인포에 따르면 11월 분양가 상한제 적용이 예정된 주요 단지는 총 7곳이다.
서울 강남권 대규모 재건축부터 시흥거모·부천대장 등 수도권 공공주택지구, 지방 공공·민간분양까지 다양하며 일반분양 물량은 5205가구로 집계됐다.
분양가 상한제 인기는 높다.
부동산 프롭테크 기업 직방이 올해 1월 1일부터 9월 18일까지 입주자 모집공고를 낸 단지를 분석한 결과 분양가 상한제가 적용된 단지 평균 청약 경쟁률은 10.8대 1이다.
미적용 단지 평균 경쟁률 3.7대 1보다 약 2.9배 높은 수준이다.
업계에서는 원자재 가격과 인건비 상승 등으로 새 아파트 분양가가 꾸준히 오르는 상황에서 가격 제한을 받는 분양가 상한제 단지의 상대적인 가격 경쟁력이 높아지고 있다는 분석이다.
11월 공급을 앞둔 주요 분양가 상한제 단지들에도 관심이 쏠린다.
가장 큰 관심을 받는 곳은 현대건설이 서울 서초구 반포동 반포주공1단지 1·2·4주구를 재건축해 공급하는 '디에이치 반포124'다.
지하 5층~지상 최고 35층, 50개 동, 총 5007가구 규모로 이 가운데 1801가구가 일반분양된다.
일반분양 물량은 전용 59·80·84㎡로 구성됐다.
경기도에서는 계룡건설이 시흥거모 공공주택지구 B-5블록에 공급하는 '엘리프 시흥 더프라임'이 공급을 앞두고 있다.
지하 2층~지상 최고 25층, 4개 동, 전용 84㎡ 단일 평면 총 338가구 규모로 이 가운데 304가구가 일반분양된다.
같은 시흥거모 공공주택지구에서는 LH가 A4블록을 공급할 예정이다.
전용 55·59㎡ 총 340가구가 공급된다.
의정부에서는 한국토지주택공사(LH)가 의정부법조타운 공공택지지구 S3블록을 공급한다.
총 732가구 가운데 544가구가 일반분양 물량으로, 전용 59·81㎡로 구성된다.
이밖에도 화성에서는 780가구 규모 병점복합타운 주상복합 1블록이, 부천시 부천대장 공공주택지구 A-2블록에 '부천대장 하우스토리 디센트'가, 전북 고창군 고창읍 덕산지구 B2·B3블록에는 '고창 데시앙'이 공급에 나설 예정이다.

May 2026 Construction permit granted for 40M Miera Rezidences in Riga The developers of the new residential project Miera Rezidences – Invego and Reterra – have received the construction permit, marking a significant milestone for the 40 million euros development on Miera Street 75.
Miera Street is a historically built and densely developed urban area where new residential projects are very rare.
“We are pleased to confirm that Miera Rezidences has received its construction permit, allowing us to move confidently into the next stage of development,” says Kristjan Thor Vähi, CEO of Invego.

“The Miera district is among Riga’s most desirable areas, so it’s no surprise that interest in this project has been exceptionally high from the very beginning, and securing the permit brings us one step closer to delivering a modern, high quality residential environment in one of Riga’s most charming neighborhoods.” Reigo Randmets, CEO of Reterra, notes that the focus now shifts to choosing the right construction partner: “We are in the process of evaluating proposals from several strong market players and we expect to finalize the selection and announce the results soon.

Our priority is quality and long-term reliability, which is why it’s essential for us to align with a partner who shares our standards and vision, ensuring that Miera Rezidences is delivered at the highest level.” The architectural concept was created through an architectural competition and developed by Latvian architecture firm Tectum.
The residential complex will offer 172 modern, energy efficient apartments with 2.8-meter ceilings, floor to ceiling windows, spacious balconies or terraces, and landscaped inner yard.
The project will be built in two phases, with construction scheduled to begin in 2026.
Miera Rezidences has already attracted remarkable public attention.

Even before the project’s official launch, nearly a thousand people had pre-registered their interest, with strong demand for two- and three-room apartments, as well as homes with private gardens and terraces.
The project’s location – with its greenery, lively cultural scene, great views, and the distinct charm of Miera Street – continues to be one of its strongest advantages.
Invego and Reterra are among the most active residential developers in Latvia, with several large-scale projects currently underway.

In Riga, the companies have jointly delivered the now completed Parka Kvartāls and are developing Skanstes Rezidences and Miera Rezidences , while Invego independently leads the development of Torņakalna Terases , Nordale and Vītolu Parks .
Outside the capital, Invego is building the extensive Mārupe residential area Mārupes Sirds and the row house district Vide Ādaži .

Kalaranna Kvartal, located at Kalaranna 8, consists of twelve 4-5-storey buildings on nearly six hectares.
The area was developed in two stages.
An integral part of the residential quarter is well-thought-out landscape architecture and a beach promenade that largely preserves the existing natural environment.
During the development, twelve buildings were completed, delivering 387 apartments, along with commercial premises and an underground car park.
The area also features Kalaranna Park, offering a variety of leisure opportunities, and a central squares connecting the buildings.
The final stage of the development was completed at the end of 2025, and the entire Kalaranna Kvartal is now finalised, with a limited number of residential units still available.
The final phase added a further 16,850 m² of gross buildable area, with 147 apartments and 4 commercial units.

Kindrali Majad Residential project Website Set between the private homes and apple orchards of Kristiine, Kindrali Majad offers modern and cosy living in Nordic-style buildings of high-quality materials and thoughtfully crafted interior details.
The development includes spacious one- to five-room apartments, studio apartments with private entrances, and even a pet washing room.
The first stage of Kindrali Majad is complete and all apartments handed over.

The second stage, Uus-Kindrali, unfolds across two buildings: the “white house” at Talli 3 / Sammu 8 is finished and welcoming its residents, while the seven-storey “black house” at Sammu 10 / Seebi 24a is taking shape beside it, with completion planned for late 2026.
Together, the two buildings of Uus-Kindrali — the white house and the black house — comprise a gross buildable area of 22,700 m², with 183 apartments and 2 commercial units.
Musketäri Majad Residential project Website Musketäri Majad is the final stage of the Kindrali Houses development and the most recently launched chapter in Kristiine City’s growth.
It extends the quarter’s green, community-centred environment with three buildings of six and seven storeys.
The development pairs contemporary architecture with considered spatial design, including homes with their own private entrances and terraces.
Built in two stages, Musketäri Majad will comprise 255 apartments across a gross buildable area of 29,500 m².
Construction began in early 2026.
In the first stage, a mixed-use building with commercial premises at Sammu 7 / Talli 1 will be completed by the end of 2027, followed by a residential building at Rivi 8 in spring 2028.
The second stage will add a residential building at Seebi 22a / 22b.

Kristiine City Residential area Website Kristiine City is one of the largest residential areas in the Baltic countries, located in the Kristiine borough, a residential area very close to the City Centre of Tallinn.
The unique project plans exquisitely integrated historical red brick buildings with the modern architecture that will arise over the hill, at the very heart of the new quarter.
The Kristiine City development will bring lively and elegant atmosphere to the barrack area.
The residential area is developed mainly to offer green living environment to families and people who prefer living outside the very centre of the city.

Developed phase by phase, Kristiine City already counts several completed stages – Tondi 51 Barracks, Marsi 6 lofts, Kristina Houses, and Ratsuri Houses – with new buildings under construction and further homes still to come.

Kindrali Houses — partly completed, under construction Set between the private homes and apple orchards of Kristiine, Kindrali Houses offers modern and cosy living in Nordic-style buildings of high-quality materials and thoughtfully crafted interior details.
The first stage of Kindrali Houses is complete and all apartments handed over.

NÜÜD Houses takes its name from its architects, NÜÜD Arhitektid, reflecting a distinctive architectural vision and a contemporary approach to urban living, with its final name to be confirmed once design is complete.
